money-path.summary: Every defect claimed in sprint_log_v0_45.md re-verifies against the working tree (line numbers shifted by 1-2: webhook P2002 catch is now webhook.js:203-206, applyMonthlyGrant read-then-SET is billing.js:102-113, cache-hit double write is search.js:139-147, outage billing default is meter.js:50 with silent swallows at citationGraph.js:64-67/95/132-135/215-217, unthrottled 401 path search.js:167 vs 255 and meter.js:32 vs 37). But the sprint log misses the structural problem: the dollar chain is broken at both ends. On the web, the SPA runs adapters client-side and never calls /api/search (only the admin GoldSetHarness does), BillingContext.deduct is a no-op, and no client code gates sources by tier, so a $10 Pro subscription changes nothing a browser user experiences; credits are only spendable through an API key, and there is no UI that mints one. Free users never receive the advertised 20/month (applyMonthlyGrant is called only from Stripe renewal events) and are seeded with 10. Pack buyers are never moved to plan=machine, so a $200 buyer gets core-only sources at 30 req/min. On top of that, a paying API caller can be charged a full credit for a search that fanned out to zero adapters (circuit-open or keyed-env-missing set → computeCoverage([],[]) = "full"), is charged full when settle/refund throw after fan-out, and gets billed for cache hits that ignore the requested cite formats. The webhook parses invoice lines with the pre-basil `line.price` shape and handles no refund/dispute/async-payment events. Nothing here should take real money until at least the P0/P1 items are closed.

findings.title: Subscriptions and credits buy nothing on the web: SPA never meters, never tier-gates, and has no API-key UI
findings.claim: A Pro/Student subscriber or pack buyer receives no usable entitlement: browser searches are unmetered and un-tiered, and the only metered surface (/api/search via API key) has no customer path to a key.
findings.evidence: src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx:58-59 `deduct` is a no-op ('spend goes through the server'); grep 'api/search' in src/ (excluding adapters) matches ONLY src/components/admin/GoldSetHarness.jsx:52,97 — the public search hook never calls the metered endpoint; grep 'tier|allowedSourceIds|CORE_SOURCE_IDS' in src/ finds no gating (App.jsx:61 uses tier only for the PricingPanel 'Current' badge); api/_shared/plans.js:8 says tier restricts 'which sources it may search' but that is enforced only in api/search.js:205; keys minting exists only server-side (api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:50-67) with no client caller.
findings.impact: Any Stripe charge is disputable as 'paid for nothing': the customer sees identical search behaviour before and after paying. Pricing copy 'All 22 databases' / '1,000 searches every month' (src/constants/pricing.js:41-45,57-61) describes an entitlement the product does not deliver on the web.
findings.fix_hint: Decide the product contract before charging: either (a) route browser searches through /api/search with session auth and tier/credit enforcement, or (b) ship the API-key management UI and re-word plans as API entitlements. Do not enable Stripe prices until one is done.

findings.title: Free users never receive the advertised 20 credits/month; seed is 10 and no grant path exists outside Stripe renewals
findings.claim: applyMonthlyGrant is invoked only from the Stripe webhook on invoice.paid/payment_succeeded, so users without a subscription get the schema seed of 10 credits once and never the FREE_MONTHLY_GRANT of 20.
findings.evidence: grep applyMonthlyGrant across api/ src/ scripts/ vercel.json → sole caller api/stripe/webhook.js:167 inside `if (RENEWAL_EVENTS.has(event.type) && userId)` (webhook.js:159); vercel.json has no crons; prisma/schema.prisma:32 `total_credits Decimal @default(10)` (unchanged since commit 03baf75 per `git log -S"@default(10)"`); api/_shared/plans.js:23 FREE_MONTHLY_GRANT = 20; src/constants/pricing.js:25,28 '20 searches / month' / '20 searches every month'.
findings.impact: Free-tier copy is false; the only free-tier API user ever gets 10 credits total. Also the free→paid funnel ('you used your 20, upgrade') can never fire correctly.
findings.fix_hint: Either seed @default(20) and add a lazy grant (in resolveApiKey/credits handler: if credits_period != current month → applyMonthlyGrant(FREE_MONTHLY_GRANT)) or a daily sweep; and align pricing.js with whatever is chosen.

findings.title: Pack buyers are never assigned plan=machine: $10–$200 buyers stay on free (core-only sources, 30 req/min)
findings.claim: The checkout.session.completed branch only increments credits for a pack; it never sets User.plan, and no code anywhere assigns 'machine', so PAYG buyers keep tier 'core' and the free rate limit.
findings.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:137-140 pack branch only does `total_credits: { increment }`; webhook.js:141-150 plan is set only when `getPlan(planId).subscription`; grep for 'machine' assignment across api/ src/ → only the definition at api/_shared/plans.js:62-71 (tier 'all', max 300/min, payg:true); api/search.js:205 `allowedSourceIds(identity.plan, …)` and api/_shared/apiAuth.js:82 `plan: getPlan(row.user?.plan)` derive entitlement from User.plan.
findings.impact: A $200 / 300k-credit buyer gets 4 sources at 30 req/min (300k credits would take ~7 days of continuous max-rate calls) while the panel copy sells 'the grounding API'. Disputable.
findings.fix_hint: In the pack branch set `plan: 'machine'` when the user's current plan is 'free' (never downgrade a subscriber), or drop the machine plan and make packs tier-neutral with copy that says so.

findings.title: Charged a full credit for a search that fans out to ZERO adapters (circuit-open or keyed-env-missing selection)
findings.claim: When every requested source is dropped by the circuit-breaker or the keyed-env guard, `adapters` is empty; computeCoverage([], []) yields coverage 1 / failedCount 0 → band 'full', so settle charges 100% for count:0 with no error.
findings.evidence: api/search.js:214-218 only guards `selectedIds`; :228-231 drops keyed sources whose env is unset; :238-239 drops circuit-open adapters; no empty-check on `adapters` before :286 preAuthorize; api/_shared/coverage.js:51-56 `total=0 → attrition 0 → coverage 1`, :35-36 `bandFor(1,0) → 'full'`; api/_shared/adapterHealth.js:24 threshold 5 consecutive failures per instance. Same class in api/_shared/citationGraph.js:55,80,102,195 where an open circuit returns null/[] with zero upstream calls, and meter.js:50 bills band 'full'.
findings.impact: Customer pays for an answer the server never attempted; response says coverage:'full', count:0 — indistinguishable from 'no match'. Directly contradicts the 'never sell a blind answer' billing philosophy and is easy to demonstrate in a dispute (e.g. ?sources=EUROPEANA while EUROPEANA_API_KEY is unset).
findings.fix_hint: If `adapters.length === 0` return 400/503 before preAuthorize (or treat as band 'limited'); in coverage.js make total===0 map to 'limited'; in citationGraph surface circuit-open as a failed leg (sprint T5).

findings.title: settle()/refund()/getBalance ordering: a DB error after fan-out charges the full pre-auth and returns 500
findings.claim: The refund-on-throw try/catch covers only the fan-out; if settle (or the refund inside the catch) throws, the exception escapes the handler, the pre-authorized credit is never returned, and the client gets a 500.
findings.evidence: api/search.js:292-376 try/catch wraps fan-out only; :380 `settle(...)` runs outside it and settle→refund does `prisma.user.update` (api/_shared/billing.js:42-45, 58) with no try/catch; :374 `await refund(...)` inside the catch can itself throw; identical shape in api/_shared/meter.js:55-63 (refund at :58, settle at :61 outside the try). Only getBalance is guarded (billing.js:67-75). Sprint T1/T2 only addresses platform kills, not JS throws in the settle leg.
findings.impact: Under DB flakiness (the exact condition seen 2026-09-01 with Supabase paused) every request charges 1 credit and returns 500 — 'never bill a failed search' is violated in code, not just by hard kills.
findings.fix_hint: Wrap settle in try/catch that on failure attempts refund and returns 500; make refund best-effort with logging; include this in the T1 journal work so orphaned pre-auths are reconciled.

findings.title: Pro subscriber holding a pack balance receives zero subscription credits; mid-month upgrades receive no grant
findings.claim: applyMonthlyGrant tops up only when balance < grant, and stamps credits_period regardless, so (a) a user with ≥1000 purchased credits gets nothing for their $10/mo, and (b) a second invoice in the same calendar month (upgrade proration) is silently skipped.
findings.evidence: api/_shared/billing.js:107 `if (!u || u.credits_period === period) return { granted:false }`; :110 `if (u.total_credits.lessThan(floor)) data.total_credits = floor` — grant is a floor, not an increment; webhook.js:166 `period = periodOf()` uses the webhook processing month, not the invoice period; pricing.js:44,61 sell '500/1,000 searches every month' with no non-stacking disclosure. Sprint T9 treats this as a copy fix only.
findings.impact: A customer who buys a pack then subscribes (the panel invites both) pays $10 recurring for nothing but the 'all' tier; a Student→Pro upgrade on the 15th pays prorated Pro and stays at 500. Both are clean Stripe disputes.
findings.fix_hint: Track the allowance separately (e.g. `monthly_credits` column reset to grant per invoice, spent before purchased credits) or make the grant an increment keyed on the Stripe invoice id instead of calendar month.

findings.title: Webhook reads pre-basil `line.price.id`; on a 2025-03-31+ API version the first-invoice grant can resolve to the FREE allowance
findings.claim: priceIdFromInvoice depends on `lines.data[].price` / `.plan`, both removed from Invoice Line Items in Stripe API 2025-03-31.basil; on such a webhook version planIdForPriceId returns null and the code falls back to User.plan, which is still 'free' if invoice.paid arrives before checkout.session.completed.
findings.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:41-44 reads `l.price.id || l.plan.id`; :160-164 fallback `planId = u?.plan || 'free'`; :165-167 grants monthlyGrantFor('free')=20 and stamps credits_period; :141-150 checkout branch later sets plan 'pro' but grants nothing. node_modules/stripe/cjs/apiVersion.js:5 pins '2025-02-24.acacia' for outbound REQUESTS only — webhook payload shape follows the endpoint/account API version (Stripe changelog 'invoice-pricing-configurations': `price` and `plan` fields are no longer available on Invoice Line Items; replace with `pricing.price_details.price`). Account/endpoint API version NOT verifiable from here (inference).
findings.impact: If the Stripe account was created after March 2025 (likely for a project that started May 2026) the very first Pro invoice grants 20 credits instead of 1000 and the month is locked; subsequent renewals then grant the correct plan only because User.plan has been set by then.
findings.fix_hint: Read `line.pricing?.price_details?.price` first, then `line.price?.id`; pin the webhook endpoint API version in the Stripe dashboard and record it in webhook.js; add `line.parent?.subscription_item_details` handling if needed.

findings.title: Cache key omits `cite` formats: a cache hit is billed but ignores the caller's requested citation formats
findings.claim: cacheKey excludes `cite`, and the cached `results` were rendered with the ORIGINAL caller's citeFormats, so a later caller requesting cite=bibtex,ris pays the same charge and receives cards without those fields (or with someone else's).
findings.evidence: api/search.js:265-271 cacheKey({query,sources,limit,authors,format}) — no citeFormats; api/_shared/cache.js:28-35 confirms the key inputs; api/search.js:405 `renderCard(r, citeFormats)` runs only on the miss path; :412-423 caches the rendered `results`; :275-280 hit path returns `...cached` unchanged after charging via chargeForBand.
findings.impact: Paid response does not match the request contract; MCP/agent callers relying on bibtex/ris will see intermittent absence depending on who searched first within the 6h TTL.
findings.fix_hint: Either include `cite` in the cache key, or cache the pre-render `limited` records and render per request (preferred — one cache entry, correct output).

findings.title: No handling of refunds, disputes, or delayed-payment completion: credits are granted on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status
findings.claim: The webhook grants pack credits/plan on checkout.session.completed unconditionally and ignores charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/failed, so a refunded or disputed purchase keeps its credits and a delayed-notification payment is fulfilled before funds arrive.
findings.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:124-152 no `obj.payment_status` check; :34 RENEWAL_EVENTS and the type checks at :124,159,173,186,193 are the full handled set; Stripe fulfillment docs: 'Check the payment_status property to determine if it requires fulfillment' and delayed methods 'generate a checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded event when payment succeeds later'. Whether delayed methods are enabled on the account is unknown (inference on that half).
findings.impact: Operator issues a refund in the dashboard → customer keeps 10k–300k credits (double loss); a lost dispute likewise. Delayed-method buyer (if enabled) gets credits on 'unpaid'.
findings.fix_hint: Gate the pack grant on `payment_status === 'paid'`; handle async_payment_succeeded identically; on charge.refunded / dispute funds_withdrawn decrement credits (clamped at 0) and log; document a manual clawback procedure until then.

findings.title: Sprint-log claims re-verified: P2002 over-broad catch, applyMonthlyGrant lost update, cache-hit 2 writes, outage-billed empty answers, unthrottled 401 path, vestigial ApiKey.plan — all CONFIRMED (line numbers shifted)
findings.claim: Every defect in sprint_log_v0_45.md holds against the current tree; the only corrections are line numbers and the unique-column citation.
findings.evidence: P2002 catch: webhook.js:203-206 (log said 202-206) swallows any P2002 while the tx also writes uniques at webhook.js:126 (stripe_customer_id, schema.prisma:26 — log said 27) and :147 (stripe_subscription_id, schema.prisma:39). applyMonthlyGrant read-then-absolute-SET: billing.js:103-111 (findUnique) → :110-111 (`data.total_credits = floor` + update) — a concurrent pack increment (webhook.js:139) between them is erased. Cache-hit double write: search.js:139-147 preAuthorize + settle. Outage billing: meter.js:50 `band='full'`; citationGraph.js:64-67,95,132-135,215-217 swallow; idResolve convertChunk returns [] on fetch failure/429 body (src/lib/idResolve.js:~121-127). 401 unthrottled: search.js:167 auth before :255 limiter; meter.js:32 before :37; checkRateLimit imported only by those two files. ApiKey.plan: written keys.js:63, displayed keys.js:24, never read for entitlement (apiAuth.js:67,82).
findings.impact: Sprint plan is sound as written; nothing needs re-planning, but T3 and T4 remain the highest dollar-risk-per-hour items and should not be deferred behind T1.
findings.fix_hint: Execute T3 and T4 first as the log suggests; update the log's line refs (webhook 203-206, schema 26/39, billing 102-113) before execution so acceptance greps match.

findings.title: Student plan is unpurchasable and the UI dead-ends: nothing ever sets is_student_verified
findings.claim: checkout returns 403 needs_student_verification for every user because no code path, admin tool, or provider writes is_student_verified; the PricingPanel shows the raw error with no verification route.
findings.evidence: grep is_student_verified|student_verified_at across api/ src/ scripts/ mcp/ → only the READ at api/checkout.js:59-60; prisma/schema.prisma:36-37 columns exist with @default(false); src/components/Panels.jsx:203 `setNotice(res?.error || …)` just displays 'Student verification required before subscribing'; pricing.js:49 CTA 'Verify & subscribe'.
findings.impact: A public plan that cannot be bought; users who try see an unactionable error. Also means the $5 rail has never been exercised end-to-end.
findings.fix_hint: Hide the Student card until a verification path exists (or add an admin toggle handler under api/user/[resource].js that sets is_student_verified for allowlisted admins).

findings.title: Rate limit is per API key: a user with 10 active keys gets 10x their plan's burst cap
findings.claim: checkRateLimit is keyed on identity.keyId, and each user may hold 10 active keys, so the per-plan max is effectively multiplied by 10.
findings.evidence: api/search.js:255 and api/_shared/meter.js:37 `checkRateLimit(identity.keyId ?? clientIp(req), identity.plan)`; api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:53-55 cap is 10 active keys per user; ratelimit.js:41 key = `oc:rl:${identity}:${epoch}`.
findings.impact: Free plan 30/min becomes 300/min against upstream polite pools; 'Priority rate limits' (pricing.js:63) is not a real differentiator.
findings.fix_hint: Key the limiter on userId (fall back to keyId only for the master key).

findings.title: ApiUsage table is never written; there is no per-key usage record for support or disputes
findings.claim: The api_usage rollup declared as the analytics record has no writer anywhere, so the only trace of a spend is the mutated balance.
findings.evidence: grep apiUsage|api_usage across api/ src/ scripts/ → no matches outside prisma/ (schema.prisma:160-170, migration 20260530120000_billing:36-45); keys.js:24-27 lists only last_used_at (apiAuth.js:75-77).
findings.impact: Support cannot answer 'how many calls did my key make'; compounds the missing journal that sprint T1 addresses.
findings.fix_hint: Either write an upsert per successful charge (fits inside T1's journal transaction) or drop the model to stop advertising a record that does not exist.

findings.title: Post-checkout return is unhandled: balance/tier stay stale until a full reload
findings.claim: The success_url `/?checkout=success` (checkout.js:110) is not read anywhere in the client, and BillingContext only refetches on auth status/user id change.
findings.evidence: grep 'checkout=success|checkout' in src/App.jsx, src/components/*.jsx, src/hooks/*.js → no handler; BillingContext.jsx:31-56 effect deps `[status, user?.id]` only.
findings.impact: Buyer returns to an unchanged UI with old credit count — the first impression after paying is 'nothing happened', which drives refund requests.
findings.fix_hint: On mount, if `checkout=success` is present, poll /api/credits a few times over ~10 s and show a confirmation toast; strip the param.

findings.title: Concurrent first checkouts create duplicate Stripe customers; renewals under the orphaned customer never map to the user
findings.claim: Two parallel POST /api/checkout calls from a user with no stripe_customer_id both create a Customer; the last write wins, and any subscription created on the other customer resolves to no user on invoice events.
findings.evidence: api/checkout.js:86-98 read-then-create-then-update without a guard; api/stripe/webhook.js:63-73 resolveUserId falls back to `stripe_customer_id` lookup for invoice/subscription events (no client_reference_id there); F-416 path at webhook.js:109-115 only logs.
findings.impact: Rare (double-click), but the outcome is a paying subscriber who never receives monthly grants and whose cancellation never downgrades.
findings.fix_hint: Use `stripe.customers.create` with an idempotency key of the userId, or search existing customers by metadata.userId before creating; also make webhook.js:126 conditional on the column being null.

security-abuse.summary: The authenticated surfaces are in decent shape: in-process getSession (api/_shared/auth.js:70-106) parses the __Secure-/plain cookie names correctly, enforces expiry, and fails CLOSED when the DB is down (live: a forged cookie → 401 while Supabase is paused); x-forwarded-host spoofing is neutralised by Vercel (live probe); Stripe webhook rejects unsigned bodies (400); no secrets or credentials are present in tracked files or git history (only the two admin Gmail addresses in .env.local.example, which are ALSO baked into the public JS bundle). The real exposure is on the UNAUTHENTICATED edge: /api/proxy is an unmetered, unthrottled bandwidth relay (live: 895 KB from loc.gov per request in 1.2 s) that can exhaust the Vercel Hobby transfer cap and take the whole site down, and the "internal-origin" guard on the keyed DPLA/Smithsonian shim routes is defeated by a single spoofed Sec-Fetch-Site header from curl (live-confirmed: real results returned). Metering has three abuse levers: DB lookups/writes run before rate-limiting, `?key=` puts bearer keys into URLs/logs, and the `;` multi-term syntax gives an unbounded upstream fan-out multiplier per credit. The Dependabot @auth/core 0.37.4→0.41.3 bump IS security-motivated (CVE-2026-73420 critical, CVE-2026-73418, GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279), but none of the three is exploitable in this config (no Email provider, no getToken, single OAuth provider) — so it is a P3 hygiene bump that must NOT be taken via PR merge (would regress prod to pre-v0.44). No new Prisma 6.x or stripe-node 17.x advisories found.

findings.title: /api/proxy is an unauthenticated, unthrottled bandwidth relay that can exhaust the Hobby transfer cap (site-wide outage)
findings.claim: The Edge proxy accepts any GET/POST from anyone, applies no rate limit or size cap, and streams the full upstream body back with ACAO:*; a script can pull multi-hundred-KB responses from 22 allowlisted hosts through Vercel's egress until the Hobby Fast-Data-Transfer quota (100 GB/mo) is hit and Vercel pauses the deployment — taking /api/search, auth and the SPA down with it.
findings.evidence: api/proxy.js:57-126 — handler has no auth, no limiter, no Content-Length cap; `return new Response(upstreamRes.body, ...)` (line 123) streams whatever the upstream sends. Live: `curl -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}" "https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=https://www.loc.gov/collections/?fo=json"` → `200 895612 1.185977`. `curl .../api/proxy?url=https://www.loc.gov/robots.txt` → 200 (arbitrary paths). `curl -X POST -d aaaa .../api/proxy?url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/` → 405 (upstream reached; POST bodies relayed, line 111-113). ~112k such requests ≈ 100 GB; one machine can do that in hours. Vercel Hobby also has no per-project WAF/rate-limit enabled (none configured in vercel.json:1-30).
findings.impact: Single attacker can knock the entire production deployment offline for the rest of the billing month (Hobby pauses on overage); paid API customers lose availability; additionally the relay lets third parties attack gallica/loc.gov/openlibrary from Vercel IPs, risking IP bans that break those SPA adapters for every user.
findings.fix_hint: Gate /api/proxy with requireInternalOrigin-style Sec-Fetch-Site check PLUS a KV/in-memory per-IP limiter; cap streamed bytes (read with a byte budget, e.g. 2 MB, then abort); trim the allowlist to the 8 hosts still called via proxiedFetch (api.dp.la, doi.pangaea.de, dpul.princeton.edu, library.oapen.org, openlibrary.org, ws.pangaea.de, www.lareferencia.info, www.loc.gov); consider Vercel Firewall rate rules.

findings.title: Keyed DPLA/Smithsonian shim routes accept a spoofed Sec-Fetch-Site header — project API quota burnable from curl
findings.claim: requireInternalOrigin trusts the literal value of `Sec-Fetch-Site` (only browsers refuse to let page JS set it; any non-browser client sets it freely), so a one-line curl obtains real keyed results from DPLA and Smithsonian on the project's keys with no auth, no rate limit and no metering.
findings.evidence: requireInternalOrigin.js:27-31 `const site = h["sec-fetch-site"]; if (site) ok = site === "same-origin" || site === "same-site"` — header value is not verifiable server-side. Live: `curl -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" "https://citation.today/api/search/dpla?q=abraham%20lincoln"` → 200 with real DPLA records (2147 bytes); `curl -H "Referer: https://citation.today/" ".../api/search/smithsonian?q=lincoln"` → 200 with real Smithsonian records; without headers → 403. api/search/[source].js:35-48 has no limiter. Smithsonian runs on api.data.gov (documented default 1,000 req/hour/key). Europeana returned `EUROPEANA_API_KEY not configured` (env unset — matches memory).
findings.impact: An attacker can exhaust the Smithsonian hourly quota in minutes, after which SMITHSONIAN throws inside the paid /api/search fan-out (search.js:323-327): every 'all'-tier customer loses that source, the coverage band drops to near-full (0.99×) until the per-instance breaker opens after 5 failures (adapterHealth.js:24), and repeated abuse risks api.data.gov revoking the key. DPLA has no published hard cap but the same relay applies.
findings.fix_hint: Treat the guard as what the code comment admits it is (soft) and add a real control: per-IP KV limiter on api/search/[source].js (reuse checkRateLimit with a small anonymous plan), plus a short-TTL server cache keyed on (source,q,offset) so repeats never reach upstream; optionally require the SPA to send a same-origin nonce minted by /api/auth/csrf.

findings.title: API-key auth performs DB reads and writes BEFORE rate limiting; invalid keys are never throttled
findings.claim: Every /api/search, /api/citations, /api/ids request with any x-api-key does a Prisma SELECT (and for valid keys a fire-and-forget UPDATE of last_used_at) before checkRateLimit runs; the 401 path for bad keys and the 400 paths for bad format/sources return before the limiter, so an attacker can drive unbounded Postgres traffic through the pgBouncer pool with no credential at all.
findings.evidence: search.js:167 `resolveApiKey(req)` (apiAuth.js:65-77: findUnique + `prisma.apiKey.update({last_used_at})`) → 401 at :169; format 400 at :197; sources 400 at :215; rate limit only at :255. Same ordering in meter.js:32-37 (authAndLimit: resolveApiKey then checkRateLimit). resolveSessionAdmin (apiAuth.js:96-102) adds a second SELECT on the sessions table for any request carrying a session cookie. Rate limiter itself is fail-open and KV-backed (ratelimit.js:45; kv.js:10-13) — if KV_REST_API_URL is unset in prod (unknown; .env.example:68 blank) the fallback is per-instance memory (ratelimit.js:20-28), multiplied by Vercel instance count.
findings.impact: Supabase free/pro pooler has a small connection budget; a cheap 401-spray exhausts it and cascades into sign-in, /api/credits, checkout and the paid search path (all share the same Prisma client) — a full-service DoS without an account. Valid free keys additionally generate one UPDATE per request regardless of the 30/min limit.
findings.fix_hint: Run a cheap per-IP KV limiter BEFORE any DB touch (apply to the 401 path); move the last_used_at stamp after checkRateLimit and debounce it (e.g. only if older than 60 s); reject malformed keys (not matching /^oc_live_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$/) before hashing/lookup; confirm KV is provisioned in prod so the shared limiter is actually active.

findings.title: `?key=` query-string API keys leak bearer credentials into Vercel request logs, proxies and browser history
findings.claim: presentedKey() accepts the customer API key as a URL query parameter; URLs (including query strings) are recorded in Vercel runtime/request logs, Web Analytics, corporate proxies and browser history, and can be sent as Referer from a browser client — none of which happens with the header form the MCP client uses.
findings.evidence: apiAuth.js:43-45 `req.headers?.["x-api-key"] || firstParam(req.query?.key)`; documented at search.js:32. Live: `curl "https://citation.today/api/search?q=test&key=oc_live_bogus"` → 401 (parameter is parsed). mcp/src/client.js:42 only ever uses the header. Inference (0.7): Vercel runtime logs display the full request path including the query string, so a key used this way is retained in the log store for the retention window.
findings.impact: A leaked key is a bearer credential to the customer's prepaid credits (no origin/IP binding — /api/search sends ACAO:* with x-api-key allowed, search.js:150-152); support staff or anyone with Vercel log access would see customer keys in the clear.
findings.fix_hint: Drop `?key=` support (header-only) before onboarding paying customers; if a query form must exist, redact `key` from logging and document it as discouraged; consider key restrictions (allowed IPs/origins) as a later feature.

findings.title: Unbounded `;` multi-term fan-out: one credit can trigger thousands of upstream requests
findings.claim: q is split on ';' with no cap on the number of terms, and each eligible adapter runs one upstream request per term inside Promise.all, so a single 1-credit request with N terms costs N×(adapters) upstream calls — the amplifier is bounded only by URL length.
findings.evidence: search.js:250 `const terms = q.split(";")...` (no length check); :306-312 `Promise.all(terms.map((t) => runSearch(adapter, t, settings, ...)))` per adapter; 'all' tier has 24 serverSafe adapters (grep serverSafe: true → 24 files). Live: a 1,500-term q (≈3 KB URL) is accepted by the platform (returns 401 for lack of key, not 414). Same split in src/hooks/useSearch.js:43 for the browser path. Per-adapter 12 s timeout (search.js:66) does not limit request count, only latency.
findings.impact: A free-tier key (30 req/min) can generate ~30×1500×4 = 180k upstream calls/min against OpenAlex/Crossref/DOAJ under the project's OPENCITE_MAILTO polite-pool identity, getting the project throttled or blocked and degrading coverage (and thus revenue via freeBelowBand refunds) for all paying customers; also inflates function duration toward the Hobby limit.
findings.fix_hint: Cap terms (e.g. max 5) and total q length (e.g. 512 chars) in apiContract.js and enforce in search.js before auth-independent work; charge per term or reject over-cap with 400; mirror in useSearch.

findings.title: Admin allowlist emails are shipped in the public JS bundle and tracked in the repo
findings.claim: VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS is inlined into the client bundle by design, and the real values are also committed in .env.local.example, so the exact Google accounts that unlock the unmetered admin plan, origin-revealing ?debug=1 and the admin console are public — the entire admin boundary is 'control of one of two named Gmail accounts'.
findings.evidence: src/lib/admin.js:3 `import.meta.env.VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS` (build-time inline). Live: `curl https://citation.today/assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js | grep -oE "[a-z0-9._-]+@gmail\.com"` → shahbaz.citationtoday@gmail.com, zabhahs11@gmail.com. Tracked: .env.local.example:6 same two addresses; docs/wiki-gh/99-Archive/architecture_report_v0_19.md:153. Server gate apiAuth.js:39-40 reads the same var at Node runtime (Vercel exposes all project env vars to functions, so it does work — established memory confirms admin path functions) and grants plan=admin on any DB session whose email matches (apiAuth.js:100-101).
findings.impact: Targeted phishing / OAuth-consent attacks against two known Google accounts; compromise of either yields unmetered all-tier search, origin-revealing debug output (breaks the product's origin-blind promise) and admin console access. Low likelihood today (zero traffic) but permanent once indexed.
findings.fix_hint: Move the allowlist server-side only (ADMIN_EMAILS, non-VITE) and have the client learn `isAdmin` from /api/credits (`tier: "admin"`) instead of a baked list; replace real addresses in .env.local.example with placeholders; enforce 2-step verification on the admin Google accounts.

findings.title: @auth/core 0.37.4 carries three July-2026 advisories (one Critical) — the Dependabot bump is security-motivated but non-exploitable in this config; do not take it via PR merge
findings.claim: @auth/core <0.41.3 is affected by CVE-2026-73420 (Critical 9.1, magic-link homoglyph account takeover), CVE-2026-73418 (High 7.5, getToken() DoS) and GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279 (Moderate, OAuth check cookies not provider-bound); OpenCITE uses none of the vulnerable paths, so the bump is hygiene — but merging the Dependabot PR would deploy GitHub main and regress prod to pre-v0.44.
findings.evidence: package.json:15 pins 0.37.4; package-lock resolves @auth/core 0.37.4 at root AND a nested 0.41.2 under @auth/prisma-adapter (two copies). Advisories: https://better-auth.com/blog/security-update-july-2026 , https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh (Email provider + default normalizeIdentifier required), https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj (requires direct getToken() call), https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279 (requires ≥2 OAuth providers). Non-exploitability: `grep -rn "getToken\|Email(\|providers/email" api src` → no matches; api/auth/handler.js:35-59 configures a single Google OIDC provider. No 2025-26 advisories found for @prisma/client 6.19.3 (lockfile) or stripe 17.7.0 (WebSearch, no hits). Established fact: pushing to main triggers a GitHub production deploy of the pre-v0.44 tree.
findings.impact: No current exploit path; residual risk only if an Email provider or a second OAuth provider (Apple/Microsoft are stubbed in handler.js:44-54) is enabled without upgrading. The operational risk is larger: a reflexive 'merge Dependabot' click regresses production.
findings.fix_hint: Bump @auth/core to 0.41.3 (and @auth/prisma-adapter 2.11.3, mcp sdk 1.30.0) in the working tree, deploy via CLI as usual, then close the Dependabot PRs; add a repo note/branch-protection that main is not the deploy source until the v0.44 tree is committed.

findings.title: OWN_VERCEL_HOST_RE trusts any `opencite*.vercel.app` — a namespace anyone can claim
findings.claim: isTrustedOrigin() accepts every host matching /^opencite[a-z0-9-]*\.vercel\.app$/; Vercel project subdomains are globally allocated, so a third party can deploy `opencite-evil.vercel.app` and be treated as a first-party origin for credentialed CORS, checkout success/cancel URLs and the shim-route Origin/Referer fallback.
findings.evidence: auth.js:22 regex; used by setCorsHeaders (auth.js:37-42, reflects origin + Allow-Credentials:true), checkout.js:31 (baseUrl → success_url/cancel_url), requireInternalOrigin.js:33-35. Live: `curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} https://opencite-evil.vercel.app/` → 404 (unclaimed, claimable). Mitigations that currently blunt it: session cookie is SameSite=lax (node_modules/@auth/core/lib/utils/cookie.js:52) so a cross-site fetch from the squatted origin carries no cookie; modern browsers send Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site which requireInternalOrigin checks first.
findings.impact: Today: low — needs a squatted project AND a browser that omits Sec-Fetch-Site or a future SameSite=None change; then it becomes credentialed CSRF against /api/keys (mint), /api/settings (read decrypted user keys) and a checkout redirect to an attacker page.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the regex with an exact list: `opencite.vercel.app` plus previews derived from process.env.VERCEL_URL / VERCEL_BRANCH_URL at runtime, or drop preview trust entirely in production.

findings.title: `sources=` validation is an unbilled, unthrottled catalog-enumeration oracle
findings.claim: A free-tier key can enumerate the server-side adapter catalog and tier membership for free: an unknown or out-of-tier ID yields 400 before rate-limiting or pre-authorization, while a valid ID yields 200 — contradicting the 'we never echo the internal source catalog' comment.
findings.evidence: search.js:205-218 (tier intersection → 400 'No valid sources selected') executes before checkRateLimit (:255) and preAuthorize (:286), so probing is unmetered and unlimited; api/search/[source].js:40 additionally echoes `Unknown source "<input>"`. Catalog IDs are guessable from the public SPA (adapter names are shown to browser users), so the oracle mostly reveals per-plan tier membership.
findings.impact: Minor information leak (which sources a plan tier includes) and another pre-limiter request path that reaches the DB via resolveApiKey first (see pre-auth finding).
findings.fix_hint: Silently intersect (fall back to full tier set) instead of 400, or move the 400 after rate limiting; stop echoing the raw slug in [source].js.

findings.title: Keyless edge shims (gallica/opencontext/openedition) are unguarded open relays; Gallica burns an upstream call before failing
findings.claim: The three Edge routes have no origin guard and no limiter, respond with ACAO:*, and Gallica performs the upstream SRU fetch (line 24) before the DOMParser call that always throws in Edge (line 48) — so every browser Gallica search costs BnF a request and returns nothing.
findings.evidence: gallica.js:5-11, opencontext.js:5-11, openedition.js:11-17 — no requireInternalOrigin import; ACAO:* on every response. Live: `curl https://citation.today/api/search/openedition?q=histoire` → 200 with real OpenEdition docs; `curl .../api/search/opencontext?q=pottery` → 200 `{results:[],total:0}`; `curl .../api/search/gallica?q=paris` → `{"error":"Gallica timed out (8s)"}` (upstream contacted; previously 'DOMParser unavailable'). openedition.js:36-49 relays a caller-controlled `q` as a POST to search-api.openedition.org with a spoofed browser UA/Referer.
findings.impact: Third parties can hammer BnF/OpenEdition/Open Context from Vercel edge IPs under a fake browser identity → risk of IP bans that silently kill those adapters for real users; Gallica currently delivers zero value while still consuming BnF quota and 8 s of edge time per call.
findings.fix_hint: Apply the same internal-origin + per-IP limiter as the keyed shims (port requireInternalOrigin to Web Request headers); fix Gallica by parsing with a regex/fast-xml-parser or moving it to Node (or disable the adapter until fixed).

findings.title: Caller-supplied `mailto` is forwarded verbatim as the polite-pool identity to OpenAlex/Crossref
findings.claim: Any API caller can set the email that OpenCITE presents to OpenAlex/Crossref for a request, so abusive traffic (see the multi-term amplifier) can be attributed to an arbitrary victim's address or a competitor's, and cache keys ignore mailto so the same result set is served regardless.
findings.evidence: search.js:246 `crossrefEmail: firstParam(req.query?.mailto) || process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO || ...`; cache.js:27 explicitly excludes mailto from the key. No format validation of the value (any string reaches the upstream UA/mailto parameter).
findings.impact: Reputational/abuse-attribution issue with upstream providers; also a header-injection surface if an adapter ever interpolates it into a header without validation.
findings.fix_hint: Ignore caller mailto on the metered API (always use OPENCITE_MAILTO), or validate it as an RFC-5322 address and only allow it for admin identities.

findings.title: Proxy allowlist retains hosts of quarantined/dead adapters, widening the relay surface for no product value
findings.claim: ALLOWED_DOMAINS lists 22 hosts but only 8 are still reached via proxiedFetch; api.bl.uk, data.bl.uk, www.iberoamericadigital.net, search.scielo.org and openneuro.org belong to adapters quarantined in v0.38/v0.44, so they exist solely as relay targets for outsiders.
findings.evidence: api/proxy.js:7-30 allowlist; `grep -rn -A2 "proxiedFetch(" src/adapters` resolves to api.dp.la, doi.pangaea.de, dpul.princeton.edu, library.oapen.org, openlibrary.org, ws.pangaea.de, www.lareferencia.info, www.loc.gov only; src/adapters/index.js:29-32 confirms OPENNEURO/ENA/SCIELO and BDH/BL/MEXICANA are quarantined. findings.title: AbortSignal.timeout hard dependency breaks every adapter on Safari/iOS < 16 (no polyfill, no browserslist)
findings.claim: fetchWithTimeout calls AbortSignal.timeout() unconditionally; on Safari 15.x / iOS 15 it is undefined, so the call throws TypeError synchronously before fetch is issued. Every adapter (direct fetches and both proxiedFetch branches) now routes through it, so those users get an error in every section and zero results.
findings.evidence: src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:19 `return fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS), ...options });`; proxy.js:50 and :73 wrap both proxiedFetch branches; `grep -rn "[^a-zA-Z_.]fetch(" src/adapters | grep -v fetchWithTimeout\|proxiedFetch` → no remaining bare fetch (every adapter is affected). `grep -n browserslist\|target\|engines package.json vite.config.js` → nothing (Vite default target = es2020/safari14). Live bundle contains `AbortSignal.timeout` ×1 (shipped). AbortSignal.timeout shipped in Safari 16.0 (Sept 2022), Chrome 103, Firefox 100; Node ≥17.3 so the Vercel Node 24 fan-out is fine.
findings.impact: Users on iOS 15 / macOS Safari 15 (a small but non-zero share, roughly low single-digit percent of Safari traffic) see 'AbortSignal.timeout is not a function' style errors in every source and an empty results page — a total product failure for that segment with no fallback.
findings.fix_hint: Guard once: `const timeoutSignal = ms => typeof AbortSignal.timeout === 'function' ? AbortSignal.timeout(ms) : (() => { const c = new AbortController(); setTimeout(() => c.abort(), ms); return c.signal; })();` in proxy.js, or add a browserslist/`build.target` that documents the floor.

findings.title: Public API contract broken (score/lowConfidence removed) with no version field, header, or deprecation path
findings.claim: D-7 removed two documented result fields and one envelope field from /api/search in place; the contract has no version identifier anywhere, no deprecation window, and the MCP package docs/description still advertise the old shape.
findings.evidence: apiContract.js RESULT_FIELDS (lines ~92-96) and RESPONSE_SHAPE (~101-107) no longer list score/lowConfidence; `grep -n version\|deprecat api/_shared/apiContract.js api/search.js` → no matches (no versioning exists). publicResult.js:50-51 emits citedBy then citations (no score). Consumers: mcp/README.md:22 still says the envelope returns `lowConfidence`; mcp/package.json:6 description still says 'deduped, ranked'; mcp/src/schema.js:90-91 and :117-118 keep dead `lowConfidence`/`score` branches (harmless — schema is derived from RESULT_FIELDS/RESPONSE_SHAPE, so the generated tool schema no longer advertises them). docs/wiki/04-Backend-API/Search-Endpoint.md:34 documents the removal. api/_shared/cache.js: cacheKey() has no version component and DEFAULT_TTL 6h, so for 6h after the deploy cached bodies with score/lowConfidence and BM25F order were still served (expired now).

findings.fix_hint: Add `version: "2"` (or a date) to API_CONTRACT and echo it as `X-OpenCITE-API-Version`; include the version in cacheKey(); fix mcp/README.md:22 and mcp/package.json:6; delete the dead branches in mcp/src/schema.js:90-91,117-118.

findings.title: Silent-swallow: shim-route adapters ignore the route's `error` field, so the broken Gallica edge route renders as 'no results'
findings.claim: The Gallica adapter (and the OpenContext/OpenEdition/DPLA/Smithsonian shim adapters) only checks r.ok; the edge routes fail-soft with HTTP 200 + `error`, so a permanently broken upstream/route is displayed as an empty section and counts as full coverage rather than a failure.
findings.evidence: src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:26-32: `if (!r.ok) throw`; `const data = await r.json(); return { results: data.results || [], hasMore: … }` — data.error never inspected. `grep -n data.error src/adapters/extensions/{gallica,openContext,openEdition,dpla,smithsonian,europeana}.js` → only europeana.js:49 checks it. Live: `curl https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test&rows=2` → {"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"} (api/search/gallica.js:45-52 guards `new DOMParser()` and returns this body). opencontext returns {results:[],total:0,hasMore:false} for the same probe; openedition returns real results.
findings.impact: Gallica has been dead-on-arrival since the edge route shipped, yet every user who enables it sees 'no matches' instead of an error, and neither the client circuit-breaker signal nor coverage/billing (server fan-out excludes it, so no billing effect) reflects the failure; the same pattern will hide the next broken shim.
findings.fix_hint: In each shim adapter: `if (data.error) throw new Error(data.error)` (mirror europeana.js:49). For Gallica itself, replace DOMParser in api/search/gallica.js with the regex/xmlUtils approach the other edge routes use, or move it to the Node [source].js shim.

findings.evidence: `ls` root → _verify_ia.mjs, Tempia_fts.json, UsersshahbAppDataLocalTempunpaywall_probe.json, COVERAGE_VERIFICATION_v0_38.md, sprint_log_v0_38..45.md present; `ls docs/wiki/10-Sprints` → Index.md only. .env.example:34-35 AUTH_APPLE_ID/SECRET, :42-44 AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_*; `grep NCBI_API_KEY .env.example` → none. .env.local.example:6 `VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS=shahbaz.citationtoday@gmail.com,zabhahs11@gmail.com`. `grep worktrees .gitignore` → none (the four .claude/worktrees/agent-* gitlinks show as unstaged ' D', not `git rm --cached`). `git diff -- .claude/settings.json` adds `Bash(curl *)`, `Bash(node scripts/…)` and mcp__…get_deployment/list_deployments/get_project/list_teams/list_projects/web_fetch_vercel_url/get_runtime_logs to the allow list.
