findings.title: dedup.test.js and dedupHighestScore still encode score-based keeper selection that no live record can exercise
findings.claim: The retained comparator makes D-2's 'first-wins' an accident of data (no record carries `_score`) rather than a rule, and the test file asserts the opposite behaviour (higher score wins) using synthetic `_score` inputs, so the suite passes while testing a dead path.
findings.evidence: src/lib/dedup.js:136 `const keep = (r._score || 0) > (existing._score || 0) ? r : existing;`. src/lib/dedup.test.js:20 `test_merge_keeps_higher_score_and_enriches`, :37 `assert(m._score === 9 …)`, :99 'slot 0 should hold the higher-scored a', :114 'every survivor must be the higher-scored copy'. `grep -rn _score src api` outside dedup*/comments → no producer of `_score` remains. api/search.js:351-352 relies on the 0-vs-0 fallthrough for ordering.
findings.impact: If any adapter ever emits a field named `_score` (e.g. passing through an upstream score), server ordering would silently stop being interleave-first-wins; the tests would not catch it because they assert the score path.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the comparator with unconditional first-wins (`keep = existing`), rename to dedupPooled, and rewrite the four score-based tests as first-wins + field-merge assertions.

findings.title: ResultCard React.memo is a no-op: onCopy/isInLibrary props get new identities every render
findings.claim: The v0.44 memoization of ResultCard cannot bail out because two of its props are re-created on every App render.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:204 `const copyText = (text, id, style) => {` (plain function, not useCallback) passed as onCopy at :275/:366/:382; src/hooks/useLibrary.js:21 `const isInLibrary = (result) => items.some(…)` (plain arrow) passed at App.jsx:368/:384. React.memo shallow-compares props, so every card re-renders on every App state change (copied, panels, filters).
findings.impact: No correctness bug; the sprint's stated perf goal ('cards whose props are unchanged skip') is not achieved, so long unified lists still re-render fully on each copy/save.
findings.fix_hint: Wrap copyText in useCallback and isInLibrary in useCallback([items]) (or pass a Set of keys).

findings.title: allDone reveal gate now bounded but multi-stage adapters can still blank the list for 30–45 s
findings.claim: resultsReady = hasSearched && allDone is pre-existing (v.31), not a v0.44 regression; v0.44 improved it from unbounded to bounded, but the bound is per-fetch, so adapters with sequential fetch stages can hold the entire results list (unified or source view) for multiples of 15 s.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:168-175 allDone requires every enabled adapter to have loading:false; :340 renders only a 'Searching sources…' placeholder until then. FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 (proxy.js:12). Sequential stages: ncbi.js:53 esearch then :61 esummary/efetch (2 stages → 30 s worst); wikidata.js:50 list=search, :67 wbgetentities, :90 label batch (3 stages → 45 s); met.js search then object fetches (2 stages). Defaults: src/adapters/index.js:98-99 `isAdapterDefaultEnabled = category === CORE` → only the 4 single-stage core adapters are on by default, so default users are bounded at ~15 s; users who enable extensions are bounded at up to 45 s. Server fan-out is separately bounded at ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_MS = 12000 (api/search.js:66).
findings.impact: A single slow extension source delays every result on screen for up to 45 s with no partial rendering; default-config users are capped at 15 s. Not a regression — before v0.44 the same gate waited forever on a hung adapter.
findings.fix_hint: Either use one AbortSignal per adapter run (total budget, not per fetch) or reveal the list once core adapters settle and append extension sections as they arrive (interleave order is stable per section, so late sections only append).

frontend-funnel.summary: The web app has no conversion lever at all: every feature the $5/$10 plans sell ("more monthly searches", "all databases") is already free and unlimited in the browser because useSearch runs all 29 adapters client-side and Settings lets anyone toggle every extension with no plan check, so the "20 searches/month" free-tier copy is false for the web and the only thing money actually buys (API credits) has no key UI, no docs page, no dashboard, and no post-checkout handling. The one path to Plans (sign-in) currently dead-ends on an unbranded Auth.js error page and the nag modal permanently silences itself before the failure is known. Student is unpurchasable by construction (403 with no verification UI), Stripe return params are ignored, and pack buyers who do pay stay on plan=free with a mislabelled "N left this month" chip. Error/empty states in the default Unified view are effectively invisible (2s auto-dismiss; Gallica's HTTP-200 error is treated as "no matches"; all-adapter failure renders the "try different keywords" hint), the results list is held hostage to the slowest of up to 29 adapters for 15s, and top-of-funnel is crippled by literal "..." JSON-LD, no OG tags, and soft-404s on every path. Ranked by revenue impact: (1) no web gating/false pricing copy, (2) no key/docs path for the paid API, (3) broken sign-in journey, (4) Student dead end + unhandled checkout return, (5) invisible error states, (6) SEO/social, (7) a11y and nag UX.

findings.title: Web app never meters or tier-gates anything; every paid feature is already free, so '20 searches/month' and 'All 22 databases' copy is false and there is no web conversion lever
findings.claim: The browser search path calls adapters directly (never /api/search, never /api/credits), and Settings lets any anonymous user enable all 25 extension adapters with no plan check, so the Free plan's advertised '20 searches every month' / '4 core databases' limits do not exist on the web and Pro's two headline features are already free.
findings.evidence: src/hooks/useSearch.js:46 `const activeAdapters = ADAPTERS.filter(isEnabled);` and :55-70 `activeAdapters.forEach(async (adapter) => { ... runSearch(adapter, ...) })` — no fetch to /api/search, no credit check; src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx:59 `deduct` is a documented no-op. src/hooks/useSettings.js:98-108 `isEnabled`/`toggleAdapter` only check `adapter.category === CORE` (to prevent turning core OFF), never a plan/tier; src/components/Panels.jsx:149 `<button onClick={() => onToggle(a.id)}` renders for every extension for every visitor. Pricing copy: src/constants/pricing.js:28 "20 searches every month", :29 "Core scholarly databases", :61-62 "1,000 searches every month" / "All 22 databases"; src/components/Panels.jsx:219-221 "Upgrade for more monthly searches and the full source library." The 20/mo grant exists only server-side: api/_shared/plans.js:23 `FREE_MONTHLY_GRANT = 20` consumed by /api/search (API-key path). Registry has 29 adapters: `awk` over src/adapters/index.js:53-96 → 29.
findings.impact: Zero reason for a web user to pay: a $10/mo Pro subscriber receives nothing they did not already have, and the free-tier copy misrepresents the product (consumer-protection/refund exposure once real money flows). Conversely, if the intent is a free web app, the Plans panel is selling a phantom and should be scoped to the API. This is the root cause of 'no revenue' more than any single bug.
findings.fix_hint: Decide the model explicitly: (a) keep web free/unlimited and rewrite the Plans panel to sell ONLY API/MCP credits (drop 'searches/month' + 'databases' bullets from human plans), or (b) route web search through a session-authed /api/search (or a new unmetered→metered endpoint) so the 20/mo grant and CORE_SOURCE_IDS tier actually apply, and gate SourcesPanel toggles on `tier` from BillingContext. Either way derive all counts/limits from api/_shared/plans.js + the adapter registry instead of hard-coding.

findings.title: No self-serve path to an API key or developer docs; pack buyers pay $10–$200 and receive nothing usable (plan stays 'free', core-only)
findings.claim: The Plans panel sells credit packs 'Bought on the web dashboard' but no dashboard, key-management UI, or docs page exists; the only mint route (POST /api/keys) has zero client callers, mints plan=free, and the Stripe webhook never upgrades a pack buyer to the 'machine' tier.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "api/keys\|/keys" src` → 0 hits. api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:8 documents POST mint, :60 `const planId = DEFAULT_PLAN_ID` (free → api/_shared/plans.js:33 tier 'core', :36 30 req/min). api/stripe/webhook.js:139 only `total_credits: { increment }` for packs; `grep -n machine api/stripe/webhook.js` → no assignment. src/components/Panels.jsx:265-267 "For developers & AI agents … Bought on the web dashboard." Live: `curl https://citation.today/docs` → 200 SPA shell (1849B), `/api/openapi.json` → 404, `/api/docs` → 404. Footer (src/components/Layout.jsx:248-256) has no docs/API/GitHub/ToS link. mcp/README.md:85 says the key is "Optional today (free tier is open)" while live `/api/search` returns 401 without a key (established fact) and :94 tells developers to run `npm run print-schemas` from a repo checkout to get the OpenAPI spec. MCP package not on npm (established fact).
findings.impact: The paid API is the only product with real gating, and it is unreachable: a developer cannot discover the endpoint, cannot obtain a key, and a pack purchase yields credits on a key-less, core-only free plan. Direct refund/chargeback risk on every pack sale; zero developer/agent acquisition.
findings.fix_hint: Ship a 'Developers' panel: list/mint/revoke keys via existing /api/keys (show plaintext once), curl + MCP quickstart, link to a served OpenAPI JSON (mcp/src/schema.js already generates one — expose via an Edge route, free under the 12-function cap). In the webhook, set User.plan='machine' (or mint keys with the user's plan) on checkout.session.completed for packs. Fix mcp/README:85 and publish the MCP package or document local install honestly.

findings.title: Sign-in journey (the only door to Plans/checkout) dead-ends on an unbranded Auth.js error page, and the modal permanently silences itself before the outcome is known
findings.claim: With Supabase paused, the AuthModal's Google button starts OAuth successfully, then the callback fails and Auth.js bounces the user to a generic, unstyled /api/auth/error page with no way back into the app; meanwhile `onDismiss()` has already written `opencite_auth_prompted` so the nag never re-prompts, and AuthContext maps every failure to plain 'unauthenticated' with no error state.
findings.evidence: Live: `POST /api/auth/signin/google` with a valid CSRF cookie → 302 to accounts.google.com (OAuth starts); `GET /api/auth/signin/google` → 302 `/api/auth/error?error=Configuration`; that page is the stock `__next-auth-theme` HTML (no OpenCITE branding, no link to citation.today root). Established fact: callback hits PrismaClientInitializationError. src/components/Layout.jsx:349 `onClick={() => { signIn("google"); onDismiss(); }}` → App.jsx:127-130 `dismissModal` sets localStorage `opencite_auth_prompted` unconditionally; App.jsx:134 skips the modal forever once set. src/lib/auth-client.js:15 `if (!res.ok) return null` and src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:29-38 treat any 5xx as logged-out (no error surfaced). Nothing in src reads `?error=` on return (grep `error=` src → 0).
findings.impact: Every prospective customer who tries to sign in today ends on a dead page; those who navigate back see a logged-out app with no explanation and never get nudged again. Until Supabase is restored the entire paid funnel is unreachable, and even after restoration a transient auth failure is silent and unrecoverable from the UI.
findings.fix_hint: Restore Supabase (orchestrator scope). In-app: configure Auth.js `pages.error` to a branded route (or handle `?error=` on `/` and show a toast with retry), set the 'prompted' flag only on explicit 'Continue anonymously', and add an `error` field to AuthContext so BillingContext/Header can show 'sign-in unavailable' instead of pretending the user chose anonymity.

findings.title: Student plan is unpurchasable: 'Verify & subscribe' CTA leads to a 403 with no verification flow anywhere
findings.claim: The Student card promises a verify step, but clicking it POSTs to /api/checkout which refuses with `needs_student_verification`, and no UI, endpoint, or provider exists to set `is_student_verified`.
findings.evidence: src/constants/pricing.js:42 `requiresVerification: true`, :49 `cta: "Verify & subscribe"`; src/components/Panels.jsx:206-212 `handleSubscribe` → `goStripe(plan, { plan: plan.id })`; api/checkout.js:58-62 returns 403 `"Student verification required before subscribing"`; Panels.jsx:203 renders that string in a 10px notice. `grep -rn is_student_verified api src prisma` → only checkout.js:59-60, plans.js:110-112, schema.prisma:36, migration — no setter, no UI.
findings.impact: One of three plan cards is a guaranteed dead end; users who self-identify as students (a core persona per the README) hit a wall with no next step, and the copy promises a process that does not exist.
findings.fix_hint: Hide the Student card (or badge it 'coming soon' with a waitlist mailto) until a verification provider (SheerID/manual upload+admin approval) exists; when built, add the verify UI before the subscribe CTA.

findings.title: Post-checkout return (?checkout=success|cancel) is unhandled: no confirmation, no next step, and the credits chip mislabels pack credits as a monthly allowance
findings.claim: Stripe redirects to `/?checkout=success` or `/?checkout=cancel`, but the SPA has zero handling for either param, so a buyer lands on the plain home page with the Plans panel closed, no receipt/next-step, and (for packs) a header chip reading e.g. '10000 left · Remaining searches this month'.
findings.evidence: api/checkout.js:110-111 `success_url: \`${base}/?checkout=success\``, `cancel_url: ... ?checkout=cancel`; `grep -rn -i "checkout=success|session_id" src` → 0 hits; live bundle `grep -o checkout=success assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js | wc -l` → 0. src/App.jsx:55 `activePanel` initialises to null (Plans panel not reopened). src/components/Layout.jsx:131-138 CreditsChip renders `{credits} left` with `title="Remaining searches this month"` for any finite balance — a pack buyer on plan=free with 10,000 pack credits sees that label (api/_shared/handlers/credits.js:51-54 returns the raw `total_credits`).
findings.impact: Buyers cannot tell whether the purchase worked, are not told how to use what they bought (no key), and the only visible signal is mislabelled; cancel returns silently. High support/refund load per sale.
findings.fix_hint: On mount read `checkout` from the URL, open a confirmation panel (success: 'Credits added — create your API key' → keys UI; cancel: reopen Plans), then `history.replaceState` to strip the param. Label the chip by plan (`credits` for machine/packs, `searches this month` for subscriptions) using `tier` from BillingContext.

findings.title: Error states are effectively invisible in the default Unified view; Gallica's HTTP-200 error is shown as 'no matches'; one slow adapter holds all results for 15s
findings.claim: In the default Unified layout the only failure signal ('N unavailable') auto-dismisses 2s after settle, per-adapter error boxes exist only in Source view, an all-adapters-failed search renders the 'try different keywords' hint, Gallica's edge-route error body is silently treated as zero results, and the list is gated on the slowest of up to 29 adapters (15s budget).
findings.evidence: src/constants/defaults.js:39 `viewMode: "unified"` default. src/components/SearchStatusBar.jsx:13-17 `setTimeout(() => setVisible(false), 2000)` after `allSettled`; error text at :35-36 is 9px. Per-adapter error UI only in src/components/SourceSection.jsx:39-43. src/components/UnifiedResultList.jsx:98 `if (allResults.length === 0 && !isInitialLoading) return null;` and src/App.jsx:353-359 shows "Few results found — try different keywords" whenever `isSparseResults` (useSearch.js:145-152 counts results only, ignores `error`). Gallica: live `curl https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` → HTTP 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"}`; src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:27-31 checks only `r.ok` and returns `data.results || []` — `data.error` is never read, so Gallica lands in the 'No matches in' chip row (App.jsx:391-405) rather than the error count. Timeout: src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:11,19 `AbortSignal.timeout(15000)`; useSearch.js:91 stores raw `err.message` (browser text 'signal timed out'/'The operation was aborted'); App.jsx:168-175 `resultsReady = hasSearched && allDone` hides the entire list until every enabled adapter settles.
findings.impact: Users see an empty or 'few results' page and conclude the search engine is bad (or blame their query) when the real cause is an upstream outage; with all 29 sources on, a single 15s stall makes every search feel broken. This is the first-session churn point before any conversion.
findings.fix_hint: Keep a persistent (non-auto-dismissing) 'N sources unavailable — details' disclosure in Unified view listing adapter names + friendly messages (map AbortError→'timed out'); treat `data.error` as a thrown error in gallica.js (and the other edge-shim adapters); distinguish 'all sources failed' from 'few results' in App.jsx; reveal results progressively or lower the budget for extensions (e.g. 8s) while keeping 15s for core.

findings.title: Source-count and pricing copy contradict each other and the code (20 vs 22 vs 29 vs 24) and the README advertises a dead domain and different prices
findings.claim: Hard-coded numbers drift: the search placeholder says 20 databases, the Plans panel says 22, the header ticker shows all 29 registered adapters, and the API 'all' tier actually spans 24 serverSafe adapters; README links opencite.app (dead DNS) and lists a roadmap with $2.99/$9.99 tiers.
findings.evidence: src/constants/app.js:17 "Search across 20 open-access databases…"; src/constants/pricing.js:15 `SOURCE_COUNT = { core: 4, all: 22 }` → :41,:45,:58,:62 "All 22 databases"; src/adapters/index.js:53-96 registry count = 29 (awk count of `_ADAPTER` lines); src/components/Layout.jsx:213 ticker renders `[...adapters, ...adapters]` = all 29; `grep -rln "serverSafe: true" src/adapters | wc -l` → 24 (this is what api/_shared/plans.js:118-122 `allowedSourceIds` intersects for the paid tier). README.md:15 `**[opencite.app](https://citation.today)**`; README.md:192 "Stripe — Starter $2.99/mo, Pro $9.99/mo" vs live Plans $5/$10; README.md:190-195 marks Identity/Billing/API as unbuilt.
findings.impact: A paying customer can point to three different promised source counts; trust and consumer-protection exposure the moment money changes hands, and the public README actively misdirects.
findings.fix_hint: Derive `SOURCE_COUNT` from the registry (`ADAPTERS.length`, `ADAPTERS.filter(a=>a.capability?.serverSafe).length`) and import it into app.js/pricing.js; delete the numeric literal in the placeholder; fix README link/roadmap/prices in the same pass.

findings.title: SEO/social top-of-funnel is broken: literal '...' JSON-LD blocks ship to production, no OG/Twitter/canonical tags, soft-404 on every path, empty SSR body
findings.claim: index.html contains three placeholder `<script type="application/ld+json">...</script>` blocks (invalid JSON) that are served verbatim in production, has no Open Graph/Twitter/canonical metadata, and the catch-all rewrite returns 200 HTML for any URL, so search engines and the AI crawlers robots.txt explicitly welcomes get nothing indexable.
findings.evidence:
index.html:28-31 (`` + three `...` scripts); live `curl https://citation.today/` shows the identical three `...` blocks; `grep -c "og:\|twitter:\|canonical" index.html` → 0; vercel.json:13 `"source": "/((?!api).*)", "destination": "/index.html"` → live `/sitemap.xml`, `/docs`, `/openapi.json` all 200 text/html 1849B; robots.txt (live) has no `Sitemap:` line; body is `
` with no prerendered content. Introduced in commit c46975e (2026-05-26).
findings.impact: Organic search and link-sharing previews — the only free acquisition channels for a zero-traffic product — are neutralised; Google's structured-data parser will report errors, and shared links have no image/description.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the placeholders with real WebApplication/Organization JSON-LD (or delete them), add og:/twitter:/canonical tags, add a static sitemap.xml + `Sitemap:` line, and prerender a minimal landing (hero + source list + API blurb) into index.html so crawlers see content; return a real 404 for unknown non-API paths.

findings.title: Auth nag UX: modal and tooltip stack on first visit, the 'after 3 searches' nag is unreachable dead code, and neither mentions Plans/API
findings.claim: A first-time visitor gets a blocking modal at 2s and then a separate tooltip at 3s (different localStorage keys); the 3-search re-nag can never fire because the blocking modal must be dismissed (which sets the same key) before any search is possible; both nags sell only 'sync', never the paid product.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:132-137 2s modal gated on `opencite_auth_prompted`; src/components/Layout.jsx:24-29 3s tooltip gated on `opencite_sync_tooltip_dismissed` (independent key). src/App.jsx:96-102 3-search branch checks `!localStorage.getItem("opencite_auth_prompted")`, but App.jsx:127-130 `dismissModal` sets that key and the modal is a `fixed inset-0 z-[100]` overlay (Layout.jsx:315-319) that must be dismissed (or sign-in clicked, which also calls onDismiss at :349) before the search input is reachable → branch dead unless localStorage throws. Copy: Layout.jsx:86 "Sign in to sync your favourites and search history", :343 "Sign in to sync your saved library and search history".
findings.impact: Interrupts before the user has seen any value (2s, pre-search), double-nags, and never communicates a reason to pay; the intended 'after 3 searches' moment (post-value) is the one that never happens.
findings.fix_hint: Drop the 2s timer, keep a single post-value nag (after N searches or on first ★ save), unify the two dismissal keys, and give the modal a second line about the API/MCP for developers.

findings.title: Accessibility basics missing on the primary funnel controls (unnamed search input with cycling placeholder, non-keyboard logo/eagle, unlabelled filters, 9–10px critical text)
findings.claim: The search box has no accessible name and its placeholder mutates every 3.5s, the h1 logo and eagle image are mouse-only click targets, FilterBar has zero ARIA (unlabelled year inputs, toggles without aria-pressed/aria-expanded), the account dropdown lacks aria-expanded, and error/checkout/coverage copy is rendered at 9–10px uppercase mono.
findings.evidence:
src/components/SearchInput.jsx:34-43 `` with no label/aria-label (`grep -c aria- SearchInput.jsx` → 0), :8-13 `setInterval(... 3500)` rotates the placeholder; src/components/Layout.jsx:183-189 `

` with placeholder-only labels, :26-39 Pill and :63-72 LangDropdown toggles without state ARIA; Layout.jsx:60,79 AuthButton toggles without aria-expanded; 9–10px copy: SearchStatusBar.jsx:33-36 ('N unavailable'), Panels.jsx:289 (checkout error notice), Panels.jsx:293 (COVERAGE_NOTE), Layout.jsx:368 modal footnote uses `text-stone-400` on `bg-amber-50`.
findings.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot reliably operate search, filters, or account; universities/libraries (the natural paying segment) routinely require WCAG 2.1 AA in procurement. The F-312 focus trap fixed the modal but the primary controls remain non-conformant.
findings.fix_hint: Add `aria-label="Search open-access databases"` (and `role="search"` wrapper), stop rotating the placeholder or move tips below the input, make logo/eagle `<button>`s, add `<label>`/aria-label to year inputs and `aria-pressed`/`aria-expanded` to pills/dropdowns, and raise critical copy to ≥12px with AA contrast.

findings.title: Outage degradation is silent: DB-down looks identical to 'logged out', settings/history/library fall back without any indicator while panel copy still promises sync
findings.claim: When the backend is down every sync path swallows the failure and the UI keeps promising account sync; a previously signed-in user simply appears logged out with no 'service degraded' signal.
findings.evidence: src/hooks/useSyncedStore.js:52 `if (!res.ok) return;` and :65-67 empty catch; src/lib/auth-client.js:15-19 returns null on any non-2xx/network error; src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx:42-46 hides the chip on non-200; src/components/Panels.jsx:419 "Signed in: settings sync to your account (encrypted server-side)." and :457-459 "Stored locally" shown regardless of state. Live: `/api/auth/session` → 200 `null` while the DB is unreachable (indistinguishable from anonymous).
findings.impact: Graceful for anonymous use (search still works), but signed-in users silently lose cross-device sync with no message, and the operator gets no user-visible signal to correlate with the Prisma errors — acceptable fallback, missing status affordance.
findings.fix_hint: Expose a `degraded` flag from AuthContext/useSyncedStore when GET /api/* returns 5xx and render a one-line banner ('Account features temporarily unavailable — searches still work'); make the panel footers conditional on that flag.

findings.title: Mobile IAP 'available via App Store at launch' copy is unreachable dead code shipped in the bundle (no native shell exists)
findings.claim: The IAP branch and its App Store/Google Play strings ship to production but can only render if a Capacitor/native shell sets a platform flag, and no such shell exists in the repo — so it is not a live dead promise to web users, just dead weight and a stale README promise.
findings.evidence: src/components/Panels.jsx:207-209 `if (rail === "iap") { setNotice(\`${plan.label} subscriptions will be available via ${store} at launch.\`)`; src/lib/platform.js:16-23 returns 'web' unless `window.__OPENCITE_PLATFORM__` or `window.Capacitor` is set; `grep -rli capacitor` → only platform.js and wiki JSON (no config/plugins); live bundle contains 'App Store', 'Google Play', 'will be available via' once each. README.md:195 lists iOS/Android under an unbuilt phase.
findings.impact: Negligible revenue impact today; minor bundle/maintenance debt and a README promise with no delivery plan.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the IAP rail (and platform.js) until a native shell is scheduled, or keep it behind a build-time flag so the strings are tree-shaken; update README roadmap.

findings.title: Perf hygiene: render-blocking Google Fonts with an unused-first font stack, Ko-fi third-party script on every load, dead Analytics component; code-splitting of AdminConsole is correct
findings.claim: First paint is blocked by a Google Fonts stylesheet pulling the full Mulish variable range (300–1000, roman+italic) even though the app's font stack prefers 'Avenir Next'/'Avenir' (never loaded), the Ko-fi overlay script is injected unconditionally, and <Analytics/> is mounted with Web Analytics disabled; the main chunk is ~99KB compressed and AdminConsole is properly split.
findings.evidence: index.html:23 `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Mulish:ital,wght@0,300..1000;1,300..1000&family=JetBrains+Mono…" rel="stylesheet" />` (render-blocking, no `media`/preload swap); src/App.jsx:219 `fontFamily: "'Avenir Next', 'Avenir', 'Mulish', …"`; src/components/Layout.jsx:260-278 KofiOverlay appends `https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/scripts/overlay-widget.js` on mount; src/App.jsx:460 `<Analytics />` (Web Analytics not enabled — established fact). Live sizes: `assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js` 318,849B raw / 98,807B compressed; `AdminConsole-DSnPXlI6.js` 10,103B served separately (lazy import at App.jsx:31-33 confirmed).
findings.impact: Slower first paint on cold visits (fonts + third-party), a floating chat widget competing with the search box on mobile, and a dead analytics script — modest, but the product has no other traffic instrumentation so the disabled Analytics also means no funnel measurement at all.
findings.fix_hint: Subset Mulish to the weights used (e.g. 400/700 + italic) and load with `font-display: swap` via preload, or self-host; defer Ko-fi until after first interaction/idle; enable Vercel Web Analytics (or remove the component) so the funnel can be measured.

adapters-retrieval.summary: The registry has 29 adapters (24 serverSafe) but live probing on 2026-09-04 shows the paid /api/search "all" tier is materially hollow: BASE (30% of the coverage denominator) is IP-denied and returns a 200 error body the adapter treats as "success, no match"; Met, PANGAEA, Thaqalayn and Open Context are silently dead the same way (wrong query flag / removed ES field / dead query param / changed API shape + Anubis bot-wall), so they never trip the circuit-breaker and never lower the coverage band. LA Referencia is Anubis-blocked because OpenCITE deliberately spoofs a Chrome UA, both loc.gov adapters were 503/timing out, Gallica's edge route is DOMParser-dead, and four adapters (Rijksmuseum, BASE, CORE, NDLI) are dead in the browser because their hosts were never added to the /api/proxy allowlist. Structurally, the API calls every adapter at offset 0 so each returns INITIAL_PAGE_SIZE=3 results: a free-tier query yields at most 12 (realistically 9) results regardless of the documented limit of 25/100, and the round-robin interleave gives Crossref's query.bibliographic hits (verified irrelevant for "ancient DNA Anatolia": personal names, landscapes, Oxford Handbook) ranks 3/6/9 while the 1043-citation OpenAlex paper lands at rank 5 -- the v0.44 "sources own ranking" thesis does not survive interleaving. Coverage economics are asymmetric by design: one OpenAlex timeout makes a free-tier query free (cov 0.40), while five dead heritage sources move the band 1%; combined with the dead-but-200 adapters, the band overstates coverage on every all-tier query. Polite-pool compliance is missing server-side (NCBI has no tool/email/api_key across 3 calls per search; Crossref drops to 1 req/s without mailto, live-verified), and the title fingerprint collapses every title-less record into one.

findings.title: API returns at most 3 results per source: `limit` (25 default / 100 max) is unreachable
findings.claim: /api/search invokes every adapter with {offset:0}, and every adapter maps offset 0 to INITIAL_PAGE_SIZE=3, so a free-tier query can return at most 4x3=12 candidates (realistically 9, since CURATED is filtered to 4 ecology ISSNs) and an all-tier query at most ~24x3=72 before dedup, while the contract advertises limit 1..100.
findings.evidence: api/search.js:315 `runSearch(adapter, terms[0], settings, { offset: 0 })` (multi-term path line 308 same); src/constants/defaults.js:4-5 `INITIAL_PAGE_SIZE = 3`, `LOAD_MORE_PAGE_SIZE = 5`; every adapter e.g. src/adapters/core/openalex.js:27 `pageSize = offset === 0 ? INITIAL_PAGE_SIZE : LOAD_MORE_PAGE_SIZE`; api/_shared/apiContract.js:11-12 `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 25`, `MAX_LIMIT = 100`, :36 'Max merged results, 1..100'; docs/wiki/04-Backend-API/Search-Endpoint.md:19 '1-100 (default 25)'. Same call shape already at 33b8b05 (git show 33b8b05:api/search.js lines 301,308), so this predates v0.44. Could not live-verify count (no API key; Supabase paused) -- code-verified only.
findings.impact: Every paid credit buys <=9-12 results instead of the 25 promised; `limit` above 12 is a silent no-op; an AI agent grounding on this API sees a 3-deep window per source, which also makes the pass-through ordering problem (next finding) unrecoverable by paging.
findings.fix_hint: Thread a per-adapter page size into runSearch opts (e.g. opts.pageSize = Math.min(limit, adapter maxWindow)) and have adapters honor opts.pageSize when present; keep the browser's 3/5 defaults. Update apiContract usage text if the cap stays.

findings.title: Round-robin interleave surfaces Crossref's off-topic bibliographic hits at ranks 3/6/9; pass-through thesis fails for the merged list
findings.claim: With no ranking layer, the API top-N is result #1 of each adapter in registry order (DOAJ, OPENALEX, CROSSREF, CURATED), so the weakest source's top hit always occupies rank 3; Crossref query.bibliographic ranks on title term overlap and hasContentMatch passes any record matching ONE meaningful term, so for a typical query the interleaved top-9 contains three irrelevant Crossref items and demotes the most-cited relevant OpenAlex paper to rank 5.
findings.evidence: Live probe 2026-09-04 (scratchpad/probe.mjs, exact adapter URLs, q='ancient DNA Anatolia'): OPENALEX top-3 = 'Ancient DNA shows domestic horses... Anatolia' (cited 70), 'Genomic insights into the origin of farming in the ancient Near East' (cited 1043), 'Ancient DNA from Mesopotamia... Anatolia' (44); CROSSREF top-3 = 'Personal Names in Ancient Anatolia' (monograph), 'Ancient Landscapes in Southeastern Anatolia' (book), 'The Oxford Handbook of Ancient Anatolia' (none about DNA); DOAJ top-3 = 'Ancient genomes illuminate Eastern Arabian population history...', 'Ancient DNA from European early neolithic farmers...', 'Eastern Mediterranean Mobility... Ancient DNA of Pigs and Cattle'. Registry order src/adapters/index.js:55-58; interleave api/search.js:115-124; Crossref query construction src/adapters/core/crossref.js:38-40 and filter :84 `mapped.filter(r => hasContentMatch(r, words))` where src/adapters/_shared/contentMatch.js:56 is `words.some(...)`. Resulting API order: 1 DOAJ-Arabia, 2 OA-horses, 3 CR-PersonalNames, 4 DOAJ-farmers, 5 OA-farming(1043), 6 CR-Landscapes, 7 DOAJ-pigs, 8 OA-Mesopotamia, 9 CR-Oxford. On the all tier the same slot rule inserts Princeton DPUL Sri Lanka pamphlets (live: 'At the service of the people in Sri Lanka...'), IA-FTS junk title 'f_2171000', and BnF 'Intercultural contacts in the ancient Mediterranean' into the top ~15.
findings.impact: A grounding API whose top-10 is ~33% off-topic on a mainstream query; on the all tier precision@25 roughly equals the fraction of sources that are relevant to the query, i.e. heritage/museum noise is guaranteed at fixed ranks. Customers pay full price for it (coverage band is 'full').
findings.fix_hint: Cheapest: require all (or >=ceil(n/2)) meaningful terms in hasContentMatch for Crossref, and order interleave lanes by source precision (OpenAlex first) instead of registry order; medium: weight the round-robin by per-source native total/relevance or restore a light RRF over native ranks (rrf.js is in quarantine).

findings.title: BASE is IP-denied upstream but counted as covered (30% of the all-tier coverage weight) and is 403 in the browser
findings.claim: api.base-search.net requires IP registration; it answers HTTP 200 {"error":"Access denied for IP address ..."} which the adapter parses as data.response undefined -> docs [] -> a successful empty result, so BASE (corpusSize 300M = 30.16% of the serverSafe denominator, larger than OpenAlex) is treated as fully covered on every all-tier query while returning nothing; in the browser proxiedFetch hits /api/proxy which 403s because api.base-search.net is not allowlisted.
findings.evidence: Live: probe2 BASE-raw -> HTTP 200 ct=application/json `{"error": "Access denied for IP address 73.118.140.113 and user agent ..."}` for both Chrome and OpenCITE UAs; prod `curl https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=<api.base-search.net...>` -> 403 'Domain api.base-search.net not allowlisted'. Code: base.js:50-55 `const resp = data.response || {}; ... docs = resp.docs || []` (no `.error` check); api/proxy.js:7-30 ALLOWED_DOMAINS lacks api.base-search.net; corpus share computed from the live registry (scratchpad/cov.mjs): BASE 300000000 / 994840000 = 30.16%. Vercel egress IPs are dynamic, so registration is not possible; that the server IP is also denied is inference (0.85).
findings.impact: All-tier customers are billed as if a 300M-record aggregator was searched; it never is. Because the adapter does not throw, the v0.38 circuit-breaker never opens and the coverage band never reflects it. If it ever did throw, the band would drop to 'partial' (0.5x) on every query (cov.mjs: 'ALL: BASE fails cov=0.6984 partial').
findings.fix_hint: Treat `data.error` as a throw in base.js; either register a static egress IP (Vercel Secure Compute) or drop serverSafe/corpusSize for BASE until it can actually be called; add api.base-search.net to ALLOWED_DOMAINS if browser use is kept.

findings.title: Met adapter is silently dead: `artistOrCulture=true` returns 0 objectIDs for every query
findings.claim: The Met search URL always passes artistOrCulture=true; live, that flag yields total=0 even for 'Rembrandt' and 'Monet', so the adapter returns [] on every query while counting as a successful source.
findings.evidence: Live 2026-09-04: `.../v1/search?q=Monet&hasImages=true&artistOrCulture=true` -> total=0; `q=Monet` -> 327; `q=Monet&hasImages=true` -> 170; `q=Monet&artistOrCulture=true` -> 0; same for Rembrandt and Anatolia. Code: met.js:22 hard-codes `&hasImages=true&artistOrCulture=true`. Wiki still marks MET healthy (docs/wiki/02-Adapters/Adapter-Health-Matrix.md:35).
findings.impact: Museum coverage advertised in the UI/dossiers is zero; on the API it is a silent no-op that still counts as covered.
findings.fix_hint: Drop artistOrCulture=true (keep hasImages=true); keep the client-side relevance filter. Add a smoke check that a known query returns >0.

findings.title: PANGAEA is silently dead since the F-116 pre-filter: ES _source no longer carries `agg-datasetname`/`title`
findings.claim: The v0.42 F-116 mitigation drops every hit whose ES _source lacks a title before the RIS fetch, but the live PANGAEA index returns _source without either requested title field, so titleHits is always empty and the adapter always returns [].
findings.evidence: Live 2026-09-04: POST ws.pangaea.de/es/pangaea/panmd/_search with the adapter's `_source` list -> 1137 hits, each _source = {agg-author, URI, agg-pubYear} only (no agg-datasetname/title); unrestricted _source key list contains 'sf-authortitle' but no 'title'/'agg-datasetname'. Code: pangaea.js:56 `_source: [... "agg-datasetname", "title"]`, :72-75 `titleHits = hits.filter(... s["agg-datasetname"] || s["title"])`, :91 `if (!doi || !title) return null`. Machine ledger marks F-116 'mitigated' (docs/wiki/_machine/_fragments/adapters.findings.json).
findings.impact: Archaeogenetic dataset coverage (the source's whole reason to exist for the target humanities/aDNA audience) is zero; counts as covered for billing.
findings.fix_hint: Request 'sf-authortitle' (or use the RIS T1 title as before) and pre-filter on that field; keep RIS for DOI/abstract.

findings.title: Open Context adapter/route is dead: API response shape changed and Anubis bot-wall blocks Mozilla UAs
findings.claim: The edge route reads `data['oc-api:has-results']`, which the live API no longer returns (response=uri-meta now yields a bare array of site links; the default JSON has totalResults but an empty has-results), and any Mozilla-UA request gets an Anubis challenge page; the browser adapter ignores the route's `error` field so the user sees an empty section.
findings.evidence: Live: prod `GET https://citation.today/api/search/opencontext?q=test` -> 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"hasMore":false}`; direct with Chrome UA -> text/html 'Making sure you're not a bot!' (Anubis); with 'OpenCITE/1.0' UA and response=uri-meta -> JSON array whose first element is {label:'APIs and Web Services', uri:'.../about/services'}; default response -> keys include totalResults=200996 but `oc-api:has-results` length 0. Code: api/search/opencontext.js:15 URL, :59 `data['oc-api:has-results'] || []`; src/adapters/extensions/openContext.js:26-29 uses `data.results || []` and never reads `data.error`.
findings.impact: Archaeological-data coverage is zero in the browser (only place it runs; not serverSafe) with no error shown.
findings.fix_hint: Re-derive the current Open Context JSON contract (likely `features`/`oc-api:has-results` under a different response profile), parse it, and surface `data.error` as a thrown error in the shim adapter.

findings.title: Thaqalayn `/api/v2/query?q=` returns 'No matches found' for any term, adapter swallows it as empty
findings.claim: The query endpoint the adapter calls does not honor `q` (even 'Allah' and Arabic 'الصلاة' return {error:'No matches found'}), and the adapter maps the error object to [] so the source is silently dead.
findings.evidence: Live 2026-09-04: `curl 'https://www.thaqalayn-api.net/api/v2/query?q=Allah'` -> `{"error":"No matches found"}`; same for prayer, salah, %D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%A9; `/api/v2/` -> 'Invalid book ID. Please use /api/v2/allbooks'. Code: thaqalayn.js:22 URL, :25 `Array.isArray(data) ? data : (data.hadiths || data.results || [])` (error object -> []). Wiki marks it healthy (Adapter-Health-Matrix.md:62).
findings.impact: The only Islamicate primary-source adapter returns nothing; counts as covered on the API (serverSafe: true).
findings.fix_hint: Check thaqalayn-api.net docs for the current search route/param (the API appears book-scoped: /api/v2/<bookId>/... ); throw on `data.error`.

findings.title: LA Referencia is blocked by an Anubis bot-wall because OpenCITE spoofs a Chrome UA, and the failure lowers the paid coverage band
findings.claim: lareferencia.info now fronts VuFind with Anubis, which serves an HTML challenge to browser-like UAs; both the server branch of proxiedFetch and api/proxy.js send a spoofed Chrome UA, so the adapter gets HTML, r.json() throws, and LA Referencia is a 'failed adapter' on every all-tier query (also blocks the no-UA and OpenCITE-UA variants, so a UA change alone is not enough).
findings.evidence: Live: direct GET with Chrome UA, with 'OpenCITE/1.0' UA and with empty UA -> HTTP 200 text/html 'Making sure you're not a bot!' (/.within.website/x/xess = Anubis); prod `https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=<lareferencia vufind url>` -> same HTML. Code: proxy.js:34-39 spoof headers; api/proxy.js:100 UA; laReferencia.js:30-32 `r.json()` with no content-type guard. Coverage: cov.mjs 'ALL: LC+CHRONAM+LAREF fail cov=0.9719 band=high' (LAREF alone: 0.30% weight).
findings.impact: Latin-American OA coverage is zero; each failure also feeds the F-208 circuit-breaker (opens after 5, then the source silently vanishes per instance) and shaves the band toward 'high' when combined with other failures.
findings.fix_hint: Quarantine LA Referencia (like BL/Mexicana in v0.44 T5) or negotiate an API path/allowlist with the operator; generally drop the Chrome UA spoof for a declared 'OpenCITE/x (mailto:)' UA and guard `content-type` before `r.json()`.

findings.title: Rijksmuseum, CORE and NDLI (plus BASE) are dead in the browser: hosts never added to the /api/proxy allowlist
findings.claim: All four adapters use proxiedFetch, whose browser branch always routes through /api/proxy, but data.rijksmuseum.nl, api.core.ac.uk, ndl.iitkgp.ac.in and api.base-search.net are not in ALLOWED_DOMAINS, so every browser call 403s. CORE and NDLI are browser-only by TOS (D7/D8) and were never allowlisted since their v0.29 introduction, so they have never worked; Rijksmuseum broke with the v0.34 keyless rewrite.
findings.evidence: Prod curls 2026-09-04: /api/proxy?url=https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/... -> 403 'Domain data.rijksmuseum.nl not allowlisted'; api.core.ac.uk -> 403; ndl.iitkgp.ac.in -> 403; api.base-search.net -> 403. Code: api/proxy.js:7-30 allowlist; src/adapters/extensions/rijksmuseum.js:175 `proxiedFetch(titleUrl...)`; coreAc.js:45; ndli.js:49; src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:63-66 browser branch. `git show 19528b3:api/proxy.js` (v0.29, when CORE/NDLI landed) already lacked those hosts.
findings.impact: Four sources the Settings panel offers (two requiring the user to paste a personal API key) can never return results in the web app; the user is told to add a key that will never be used successfully. Server fan-out for RIJKS still works (direct fetch), so the API and browser disagree.
findings.fix_hint: Add the four hosts to ALLOWED_DOMAINS (keep the https/redirect guards), or convert Rijksmuseum to direct fetch if it sends CORS headers; add a test asserting every proxiedFetch host in src/adapters is allowlisted.

findings.title: Both loc.gov adapters were failing (503 / >45s) and api/proxy has no upstream timeout, producing 504 FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT
findings.claim: On 2026-09-04 loc.gov search returned 503 after ~45s from the probe IP and the prod edge proxy hit Vercel's 25s kill (504) for the Chronicling America URL; LC_DATASETS (direct fetch, serverSafe) and CHRONICLING_AMERICA both count as failed adapters on the API, moving the all-tier band to 'high' (0.95x), and the proxy itself has no AbortSignal so a hung upstream consumes the full edge function budget.
findings.evidence: Live: `https://www.loc.gov/search/?q=cat&fo=json&c=1` -> HTTP 503 'Service-Unavailable' after 45367ms (Chrome and OpenCITE UAs; homepage HEAD 200 in 62ms); prod `https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=<loc.gov chronicling-america ...>` -> 504 'FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT pdx1::...' at 25079ms. Code: api/proxy.js:116 `followSafe(targetUrl.href, fetchOptions)` with no signal/timeout (browser side aborts at 15s via proxy.js:73, server keeps running); lcDatasets.js:26 and chroniclingAmerica.js:27. Coverage: cov.mjs 'ALL: LC+CHRONAM fail cov=0.9749 band=high x0.95'. Whether this is a transient loc.gov incident or geo/rate blocking is not determined (observed once).
findings.impact: Every all-tier query is discounted 5% while loc.gov is degraded (the intended economics, but silent), each search burns 12s of function time waiting, and the edge proxy can be pinned for 25s per hung request.
findings.fix_hint: Add AbortSignal.timeout(~10s) to api/proxy.js fetches; consider loc.gov's documented rate limits (newspaper endpoint 20 req/min) and a shared LOC client with backoff; re-probe before deciding whether to quarantine.

findings.title: Gallica edge route is DOMParser-dead in prod while a regex SRU parser (xmlUtils) already exists
findings.claim: The Gallica edge route parses SRU XML with DOMParser, which does not exist in Vercel Edge, so every Gallica browser search returns the error envelope; the upstream itself works (644 hits live) and src/adapters/_shared/xmlUtils.js already provides sruTotal/sruRecords/dcOne/dcAll used by ONB/BnF.
findings.evidence: Prod: `GET https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` -> 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"}`; direct SRU `gallica all "ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> numberOfRecords 644. Code: api/search/gallica.js:48 `new DOMParser()`, :45 comment admits it; xmlUtils.js:1-16 header says the helpers exist precisely because 'DOMParser is not reliably available in all Edge runtime contexts'. Adapter src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:29 ignores `data.error`.
findings.impact: BnF Gallica (15M items, one of the few full-text heritage sources) is dead in the only runtime it is wired to; user sees an empty section with no error.
findings.fix_hint: Replace DOMParser in api/search/gallica.js with the xmlUtils DC helpers (the Edge route cannot import src/, so inline or move xmlUtils under api/_shared); surface `data.error` in the shim adapter.

findings.title: Coverage billing is asymmetric and now overstated: one OpenAlex timeout = free query, while dead-but-200 sources are counted as covered
findings.claim: Corpus-weighted coverage makes the free tier a coin-flip on OpenAlex (25% of all-tier, 60% of free-tier weight): its single timeout yields band 'limited' (0 credits), Crossref's yields 'partial' (0.5x), whereas five heritage sources failing together move the band by 1%; and because failure is defined as 'threw', the five adapters that return 200-with-nothing (BASE 30.16%, MET, PANGAEA, THAQALAYN, OPENCONTEXT-n/a) are counted as covered, so 'full' is reported and charged for a library where >30% of the declared weight is unreachable.
findings.evidence: cov.mjs against the live registry (coverage.js computeCoverage/bandFor): FREE OpenAlex fails -> cov 0.3976 'limited' x0; FREE Crossref fails -> 0.6265 'partial' x0.5; FREE DOAJ fails -> 0.9759 'high'; ALL OpenAlex fails -> 0.7487 'partial'; ALL MET+THAQ+NU+DPUL+PANGAEA fail -> 0.9989 'near-full' x0.99; ALL every non-core fails -> 'limited' x0. coverage.js:47-48 'empty results is NOT a failure'; :18 FALLBACK_CORPUS=1 applies only to CORE/NDLI (not serverSafe, so irrelevant to the denominator). Live OpenAlex latency in probe: 4455ms vs ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_MS 12000 (api/search.js:66).
findings.impact: Revenue leaks whenever OpenAlex is slow (queries become free) yet customers are overcharged structurally because the denominator includes sources that can never answer; the band no longer measures what it claims.
findings.fix_hint: Treat 'zero results from a source whose upstream returned an error body' as failure (adapters throw on `error` keys); remove unreachable sources from serverSafe; consider capping any single source's weight (e.g. 40%) or using a query-hit-based signal instead of static corpusSize.

findings.title: NCBI E-utilities called without tool/email/api_key, 3 sequential-parallel calls per search against a shared 3 req/s per-IP budget
findings.claim: The NCBI adapter sends esearch + esummary + efetch (3 requests) per search with no `tool`, `email` or `api_key` parameters, so every server-side search consumes the entire 3 req/s anonymous per-IP allowance; on Vercel's shared egress IPs and at the machine plan's 300 req/min this guarantees 429s, and it violates NCBI's usage policy which asks for tool+email (idResolve.js does it correctly).
findings.evidence: ncbi.js:53 esearch URL, :61 esummary, :62 efetch -- none carry tool/email/api_key; grep shows NCBI_API_KEY is read only in api/ids.js:41 and api/search.js:341 (the default-off canonicalizer); src/lib/idResolve.js:29 DEFAULT_EMAIL='ops@citation.today' and :111 `email:` param -- the search adapter never received the same treatment. api/_shared/plans.js:68 machine rateLimit max 300/min.
findings.impact: NCBI throttling turns into 'failed adapter' events (3.72% weight) and, worse, IP-level blocks that also hit /api/ids; policy non-compliance risk for a commercial API.
findings.fix_hint: Append `&tool=opencite&email=<OPENCITE_MAILTO>` and `&api_key=${NCBI_API_KEY}` (10 req/s) in ncbi.js; add a tiny per-instance token bucket for eutils; consider Europe PMC (dossier Tier A) as the server-side biomedical source.

findings.title: Crossref/OpenAlex polite pool depends on OPENCITE_MAILTO being set; without it the server shares a 1 req/s Crossref pool (live-verified) and sends UA 'node'
findings.claim: Crossref and OpenAlex only get the polite pool when settings.crossrefEmail is non-empty, which on the API comes from ?mailto or process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO (unverified in Vercel) and in the browser defaults to ''; no User-Agent is set anywhere on the direct-fetch adapters, so server requests identify as Node's default UA.
findings.evidence: Live 2026-09-04: api.crossref.org without mailto -> `x-rate-limit-limit: 1, x-rate-limit-interval: 1s`; with `&mailto=ops@citation.today` -> `x-rate-limit-limit: 3`. Code: crossref.js:28 mailto conditional; openalex.js:30-31; curatedJournals.js:33-35; api/search.js:246 `process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.crossrefEmail`; defaults.js:25 `crossrefEmail: ""`; fetchWithTimeout (proxy.js:18-20) adds no UA. Whether OPENCITE_MAILTO is set in prod could not be read (Vercel get_project does not expose env) -- inference 0.6 that it is unset given no runtime evidence.
findings.impact: If unset, all API customers share 1 req/s to Crossref (and OpenAlex's anonymous pool) per egress IP: the machine plan's 5 req/s cap alone would exceed it; every extra search also doubles OpenAlex load because CURATED is a second OpenAlex call.
findings.fix_hint: Set OPENCITE_MAILTO in Vercel prod; hard-code a fallback mailto + `User-Agent: OpenCITE/<ver> (https://citation.today; mailto:...)` in fetchWithTimeout for the server branch; verify with the x-rate-limit headers.

findings.title: CURATED (4 hard-coded ecology ISSNs) runs on every API query as a 'core' source
findings.claim: The API settings spread DEFAULT_SETTINGS, whose curatedJournals is the developer's personal list (Ecological Informatics, Ecosphere, Frontiers in Marine Science, PeerJ), so every paid query issues a second OpenAlex call restricted to those journals (without the is_oa filter) and interleaves its hits at ranks 4/8/12 when they exist; it is also one of the four free-tier sources and 1/4 of the free-tier result budget.
findings.evidence: api/search.js:242-247 `{ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...envKeys, ... }`; src/constants/defaults.js:13-18 DEFAULT_CURATED_JOURNALS, :35 `curatedJournals: DEFAULT_CURATED_JOURNALS`; curatedJournals.js:23-25 and :40 `primary_location.source.issn:${issnFilter}`; plans.js:17 CORE_SOURCE_IDS includes CURATED; useSettings.js:41 same default for every new browser user.
findings.impact: Off-topic ecology papers can appear for any query; OpenAlex is hit twice per search; the free tier's '4 core sources' is really 3 + a personal journal list.
findings.fix_hint: Exclude CURATED from the API's default eligible set (opt-in via ?sources=CURATED with a caller-supplied ISSN list) and ship the browser with an empty curated list.

findings.title: titleFingerprint collapses every title-less record (sanitized to 'Untitled') into one, and merges same-title works with empty author/year
findings.claim: The fingerprint is `${normalizedTitle}|${year}|${firstAuthorSurname}`; sanitize() rewrites empty titles to 'Untitled' and heritage adapters frequently emit authors [] and year '', so all such records share the key 'untitled||' and the pooled dedup (dedupHighestScore) field-merges them into the first one (server) or drops them (browser); generic titles ('Introduction', 'Editorial', newspaper mastheads) from sources that emit no authors collide the same way. DOI normalization itself is correct.
findings.evidence: dedup.js:25-30 titleFingerprint; :136-140 merge into first keeper; src/adapters/_shared/base.js:28 `title: str(result.title) || "Untitled"`; adapters emitting authors: [] -- chroniclingAmerica.js:44, thaqalayn.js:35, api/search/opencontext.js:82, wikidata fallback; IA FTS mapFtsHit title fallback internetArchive.js:124 ('f_2171000'-style junk titles observed live); doiKey dedup.js:15-21 verified (lowercase, trims, strips doi.org prefix; note it does not strip a 'doi:' prefix or trailing punctuation). Logic-verified, not live-observed (no API key).
findings.impact: Legitimate distinct records vanish or are merged into a chimera (abstract/authors/subjects unioned from unrelated works) exactly for the metadata-poor heritage sources the all tier sells.
findings.fix_hint: Return null from titleFingerprint when the title is the 'Untitled' sentinel or shorter than ~3 tokens with no author/year; include source-agnostic secondary keys (url) before falling back to title.

findings.title: ONB and BnF SRU adapters wrap the whole query in quotes (exact phrase), so multi-word queries get near-zero recall
findings.claim: `alma.all_for_ui="<query>"` and `bib.anywhere="<query>"` are phrase searches; a typical 3-word topical query returns 0 (ONB) or 1 (BnF) records while the single term returns hundreds.
findings.evidence: Live: ONB `alma.all_for_ui="ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> numberOfRecords 0; `alma.all_for_ui="Anatolia"` -> 545; BnF `bib.anywhere="ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> 1. Code: onb.js:24, bnfApi.js:25 (both quote the raw query).
findings.impact: Two of the three national-library sources contribute almost nothing on real queries yet count as successful coverage.
findings.fix_hint: Use `all` / `and` CQL operators (e.g. `alma.all_for_ui all "w1 w2"` or per-term AND) instead of a single quoted phrase; keep phrase mode for quoted user input.
