ops-deploy-data.summary: The single largest risk is data loss, not code: the only copy of every user, API key, credit balance and Stripe idempotency record lives in a Free-plan Supabase project (org "Citation.today", plan=free) that has been INACTIVE since roughly mid/late June 2026, on a plan with zero automated backups and no off-site dump anywhere in the repo; the last proof the DB was alive is the 2026-06-10 production build log. Second, the GitHub->Vercel integration auto-deploys `main` to production (every `githubCommitRef: main` deployment has `target: production`), and the three open Dependabot PRs built green, so a single merge click regresses prod from the dirty v0.44 CLI deploy (dpl_2ZTVC6KJ) back to the v0.43.1 engine tree (28.6 MB synonyms, BM25F/RRF/semantic workers, `credits: Infinity` -> JSON null, loopback getSession, no fetch timeouts, old API contract). Third, the migration story is weaker than the wiki claims: `prisma/migrations` has NO migration for users/accounts/sessions/search_history/library_items (they exist only because prod was `db push`ed), so the disaster-recovery path of "restore backup into a fresh project and `migrate deploy`" fails on `ALTER TABLE "users"`; and `scripts/migrate.mjs` echoes the full direct connection string (password included) into the Vercel build log whenever `migrate deploy` fails - which is exactly what the next production deploy will do while Supabase is paused. No lockout/data-loss mode was found in the migrate fallback itself (it never baselines unless every SQL applied). Observability is effectively nil (Analytics unregistered, console-only logging, no uptime probe, Hobby log retention measured in hours), which is why an auth outage that started weeks ago surfaced only via the orchestrator's probes. Node function count is 8 files (Vercel reports 9) under the 12 cap; v0.45 adds no files and one daily cron, which Hobby allows.

findings.title: Supabase OpenC_Auth paused ~10 weeks on Free plan with zero backups and no off-site dump — all user/key/credit data is one policy tick from unrecoverable
findings.claim: The only persistent copy of users, accounts, sessions, api_keys, api_usage, processed_events, search_history, library_items and relevance_labels is a Free-plan Supabase project that is INACTIVE; the Free plan takes no daily backups and the repo contains no dump/backup tooling, so the pause-time logical backup Supabase holds is the sole copy.
findings.evidence: Supabase MCP get_project cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq → status "INACTIVE", db host db.cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq.supabase.co, created 2026-05-10; get_organization wxyjeuyqxeweeqgmxobf → plan "free". Last proof DB was alive: Vercel build log of prod deploy dpl_2ZTVC6KJHiFH9NKFBvdHni3q82P3 (2026-06-10 07:08 UTC) "Datasource … aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432 … 3 migrations found … No pending migrations to apply". Supabase docs (free-project-pausing): pause after ~7 days of low DB activity; restore via dashboard "up to 1 year after it was paused"; changelog 27497 (June 2024) previously set the window at 90 days and third-party 2026 guides still cite 90 days. Supabase backups doc: Free plan has no automated backups ("regularly export … db dump"); PITR requires Pro + Small compute. `grep -rln "pg_dump|db dump|supabase db"` over the repo → no matches. Runtime error 2026-09-01 "FATAL: Tenant or user not found" from the pooler is Supavisor de-registering the paused tenant (github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/30107, /35749) — consistent with pause, NOT deletion (project still listed, db host still assigned). Estimated pause date: 2026-06-17..24 (7-day inactivity after the last known activity on 06-10) → ~70-77 days paused on 2026-09-02; under the older 90-day rule one-click restore would close ~2026-09-15..22, under the current 1-year rule ~June 2027. Confidence on pause date is inference.
findings.impact: If the 90-day interpretation is the one enforced (or the 1-year window lapses unnoticed, which is how the last 10 weeks went), the only recovery is downloading the pause-time .backup and rebuilding a new project by hand; if Supabase deletes the project, every registered user, every issued oc_live_ key hash, every credit balance and every Stripe processed_events row is gone permanently. Until restore, sign-in, credits, history, library, settings sync, API-key auth, checkout and the Stripe webhook are all dead (verified by the orchestrator's 09-01 PrismaClientInitializationError).
findings.fix_hint: Order of operations for Shahbaz: (1) Supabase dashboard → OpenC_Auth → "Resume project" (or MCP restore_project); wait for ACTIVE_HEALTHY. (2) Verify with MCP list_tables / execute_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM users, api_keys, processed_events, library_items, search_history, _prisma_migrations (expect the 3 migration rows). (3) IMMEDIATELY take an off-site dump: `supabase db dump --db-url <session-pooler url> -f opencite-$(date +%F).sql` and store it outside Vercel/Supabase; add this to a weekly routine. (4) Prevent re-pause: either upgrade the org to Pro ($25/mo: no pausing + 7-day daily backups) or add a keepalive (a daily Vercel cron hitting a tiny Prisma query — Hobby allows daily crons — is enough per Supabase's "a few requests a day" threshold). What restore does NOT recover: nothing DB-side is lost within the window, but every `sessions` row will be expired (all users re-login), the pooler tenant may need a password reset if "Tenant or user not found" persists after resume, and if you end up on the new-project path the project ref changes → POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL/POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING in Vercel and the ops_credentials memory must be rewritten.

findings.title: Merging any open Dependabot PR (or any push to main) auto-deploys the pre-v0.44 engine tree to production
findings.claim: Vercel's GitHub integration deploys every commit on `main` straight to production, and `main` (33b8b05) is the v0.43.1 engine tree, so the three green Dependabot PRs are one click away from replacing the live dirty v0.44 deployment with a build that reinstates everything v0.44 removed.
findings.evidence: Vercel list_deployments: every `githubCommitRef: "main"` deployment has `target: "production"` with `githubDeployment: "1"` (dpl_9fDw3fNEtcUGL8bceJrewcvU54n1 for 33b8b05, dpl_HU914ViPrNZkaiLAdqXq7Q17Kjsw for 4beb92e, dpl_6yXNSQuRzSEzGHuA4ZTchbo4cxdw for ab75ed1, etc.). Live prod is dpl_2ZTVC6KJHiFH9NKFBvdHni3q82P3 (`gitDirty: "1"`, `actor: claude-code_2-1-170_agent`, 2026-06-10) whose build emitted `dist/assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js` 318.58 kB and NO worker chunks; `curl https://citation.today/` still references `assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js`. The Dependabot PR builds (dpl_DE31RrgR8RNxBm4GvYMTJ5hwHMEE PR#8 mcp sdk 1.30.0; dpl_94wrsdgkHC956DPsfG9wkH4st6R9 PR#7 @auth/core 0.41.3; dpl_CX5FvNDE8gX15CXuoFD84krnxB89 PR#6 prisma-adapter 2.11.3) are all state READY and emit `synonyms.worker-Dxzqs6_d.js`, `embed.worker-BES4aO53.js`, index 346.06 kB — i.e. the engine is back. Drift quantified: `git diff HEAD --stat` = 149 files, +1126/−10215; `git ls-tree -r -l origin/main -- public/synonyms` = 26 files, 28.59 MB (fetched at runtime by main's src/lib/synonyms.js:76 `fetch(`/synonyms/${letter}.json`)`); main's api/_shared/handlers/credits.js:24,42 returns `credits: Infinity` (JSON → null); main's api/_shared/auth.js getSession is the HTTP loopback self-fetch; `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000` exists only in the working tree (src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:11); main's apiContract.js still advertises `score`/`lowConfidence`; main has api/search/{bdh,bl,mexicana}.js + adapters; src/constants/app.js on main = "v.43". Schema/migrations are identical on both sides (3 migrations), so the regression is code-only.
findings.impact: A routine dependency merge silently reverts production to a slower, heavier, contract-incompatible build (MCP clients would get `score` back and `credits` null-for-admin regression), with no review gate and no rollback signal because nothing monitors prod. It also bumps @auth/core across four minors (0.37→0.41) — a change the repo's own dependabot.yml comment says has shipped breaking changes — directly into production. Additionally the next production deploy runs the migrate fallback against the paused DB (see the credential-leak finding).
findings.fix_hint: Before touching any PR: commit the v0.44 working tree to `main` (only when Shahbaz asks, per CLAUDE.md) so main == prod, then let Dependabot rebase. Until then, either close/pause the Dependabot PRs or set Vercel → Project Settings → Git → "Ignored Build Step"/disable production deploys from Git so a merge cannot auto-ship. Also mark sprint_log_v0_44.md Actuals so the state is written down somewhere other than a Vercel deployment record.

findings.title: scripts/migrate.mjs prints the direct Postgres URL (password included) into Vercel build logs on the fallback path — which the next prod deploy will take while Supabase is paused
findings.claim: `run()` logs the full command (`[migrate] $ ${cmd}`, line 34) and the fallback builds `execCmd` with `--url "${DIRECT_URL}"` (lines 59-60), so whenever `prisma migrate deploy` fails in an environment where POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING is set, the connection string with the database password is written verbatim to the build log.
findings.evidence: scripts/migrate.mjs:31 `const DIRECT_URL = process.env.POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING || ""`; :34 `console.log(`[migrate] $ ${cmd}`)`; :59-60 `npx prisma db execute --url "${DIRECT_URL}" --file ${sqlFile}`; :47-52 the fallback is entered on ANY `migrate deploy` failure, not just P3005 (comment at :52 says "likely P3005"). Trigger is live today: with the DB paused, `migrate deploy` fails (P1001/tenant-not-found) on the next production build. The preview builds (dpl_DE31…, dpl_94wr…) show the fallback firing on failure — they took the `--schema` branch only because POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING is absent in the Preview env. Vercel build logs are retained per deployment and visible to anyone with project access or a shared inspector link.
findings.impact: Database superuser credentials for the only copy of customer/billing data end up in a log store outside the secret manager; anyone who later gets read access to the Vercel project (collaborator, leaked inspector URL, Vercel support) can connect directly, bypassing Prisma, RLS-less tables and the API key hashing. Rotation would then also require touching Vercel env + any dumps.
findings.fix_hint: Never interpolate the URL into a logged string: pass it via env (`execSync(cmd, { env: { ...process.env, DATABASE_URL: DIRECT_URL } })` and `--url "$DATABASE_URL"`), or log a redacted copy (`cmd.replace(/:\/\/[^@]+@/, '://***@')`). Also gate the fallback on the actual P3005 error text so an unreachable DB fails fast instead of running four more failing Prisma invocations. If a prod deploy has already happened since the pause, rotate the DB password after restore.

findings.title: Migration set cannot rebuild the schema from scratch — base tables (users/accounts/sessions/…) have no migration, so the documented DR path 'restore into a fresh project + migrate deploy' fails on ALTER TABLE "users"
findings.claim: prisma/migrations only contains the three additive migrations (billing, relevance_labels, api_usage_fk); the tables Auth.js and the app depend on exist in prod solely because of a historical `prisma db push`, so the wiki's F-503 'a from-scratch migrate deploy now provisions every table' is false and any new-project recovery needs a `db push`/baseline step nobody has written down.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn -i 'CREATE TABLE … "users"|"accounts"|"sessions"|"search_history"|"library_items"' prisma/migrations` → no matches; migration.sql line 10 starts with `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS …` (fails with 42P01 on an empty DB); scripts/migrate.mjs:10-13 documents the db-push origin. docs/wiki/07-Data-Layer/Data-Layer.md (F-503 entry) claims "a from-scratch deploy creates every table". prisma/schema.prisma:18-134 defines six models with no corresponding migration. Migrations that DO exist match schema.prisma (relevance_labels 186-196, api_usage FK 160-170) — that part is complete.
findings.impact: In exactly the scenario the paused-Supabase risk leads to (window lapses, must restore the .backup into a new project), an operator following the wiki will get a failed migration and a half-provisioned DB; worse, migrate.mjs's fallback would then `db execute` the billing SQL, fail, skip baselining, and every subsequent deploy silently repeats the failure (exit 0) while auth 500s. No lockout or destructive mode was found in migrate.mjs against a merely paused DB (it never baselines unless all SQL applied, and all SQL is IF NOT EXISTS/guarded), but the from-scratch path is broken.
findings.fix_hint: Add `prisma/migrations/00000000000000_init/migration.sql` generated from `prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script`, made idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), placed before the billing migration, and baseline it on the live DB with `prisma migrate resolve --applied 00000000000000_init` (migrate.mjs already loops all dirs). Document the DR runbook: restore .backup with psql over the session pooler → baseline → deploy. Correct the F-503 wiki entry.

findings.title: Stripe webhook 500s during any DB outage >72h → renewals/purchases charged by Stripe but credits never granted, with no alert or replay tool
findings.claim: With Prisma unreachable the whole webhook transaction throws PrismaClientInitializationError, which is not P2002, so the handler returns 500 (line 209); Stripe retries for up to ~3 days and then stops, so any `invoice.paid`/`checkout.session.completed` fired while Supabase is paused (or during any multi-day outage) is a paid event with no ledger effect, and nothing in the codebase or v0.45 plan replays missed events.
findings.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:121 `prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { await tx.processedEvent.create(...)` — first DB touch throws on a paused DB; :203-205 only P2002 is ACKed; :207-209 everything else → `log.err` (console only, api/_shared/log.js:25) + 500. Stripe's documented retry policy for live-mode endpoints is retries over up to 3 days then the event is marked failed. api/checkout.js:86-97 also hits `prisma.user.findUnique/update` before creating the session, so new checkouts fail today with 500 (line 118) — but Stripe-initiated subscription renewals need no checkout and would still be billed. sprint_log_v0_45.md T1-T3 add a credit_events journal and P2002 scoping but no 'replay Stripe events since <ts>' path.
findings.impact: A paying subscriber (if any exist — DB counts are unknowable until restore) charged during the pause receives no credits: money taken, service dead, no email, no dashboard flag; the founder learns only from a chargeback. Same class of loss recurs on every future DB incident longer than Stripe's retry window.
findings.fix_hint: After restore: in the Stripe dashboard filter webhook events with failed delivery since ~2026-06-17 and re-send them (the processed_events unique claim makes replay safe). Structurally: add an admin `reconcile-stripe` action to the v0.45 [resource].js dispatcher that lists `stripe.events.list({delivery_success:false, created:{gte}})` and re-runs the handler; and make webhook DB-init failures return 503 with a `Retry-After` so the failure is at least categorised. Add an alert on any 5xx from /api/stripe/webhook (see monitoring finding).

findings.title: No monitoring of any kind — the auth/DB outage ran for weeks undetected; Web Analytics unregistered despite <Analytics/> being mounted
findings.claim: There is no uptime probe, no error alerting, no analytics registration and only console logging with Hobby-tier retention, so a total loss of sign-in/billing since ~mid-June 2026 produced zero signal until an external probe on 2026-09-01.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:2,460 mounts `<Analytics />` but the Vercel API returns 404 'Web Analytics not found' (orchestrator fact — the project-level toggle was never enabled, so the component no-ops). api/_shared/log.js:25-27 — `log`, `log.warn`, `log.err` are bare console calls; `grep -n 'sentry|uptime|monitor|alert'` across src/main.jsx, src/App.jsx, package.json → nothing. Vercel Hobby runtime-log retention is on the order of hours (vercel.com/docs/limits), so the Sep-1 PrismaClientInitializationError would have aged out unseen. Supabase itself emails a pause warning ~1 week before and a confirmation after; those went to the org owner and were not acted on.
findings.impact: Availability incidents are invisible; revenue incidents (webhook 500s) are invisible; the Supabase restore-window clock runs silently. Any future paying customer's first contact will be a support email, not a dashboard.
findings.fix_hint: Minimum viable, all free: (1) Vercel dashboard → Analytics → Enable (the component is already mounted). (2) External uptime monitor (UptimeRobot/Better Stack free tier, 5-min interval) with three checks that would each have caught Sep-1: GET https://citation.today/api/auth/session must return HTTP 200 with JSON body `{}` or a user (a 500 = Prisma/auth down); GET /api/credits must return 401 (a 503/500 = DB down); GET /api/search/opencontext?q=test must return 200 with `results` — plus a keyword check that the body does NOT contain "error". (3) Route `log.err` through a webhook (Discord/Slack/email) or Vercel Log Drain (Pro) for any 5xx from /api/auth/handler and /api/stripe/webhook. (4) Forward Supabase org emails to a monitored inbox and add the daily DB keepalive from the P0 finding.

findings.title: Gallica edge route is permanently dead: DOMParser does not exist in Vercel Edge runtime
findings.claim: api/search/gallica.js declares `runtime: 'edge'` and constructs `new DOMParser()` which is not available in the Edge V8 runtime, so every request returns the fail-soft error envelope and Gallica contributes zero results to every search.
findings.evidence: api/search/gallica.js:3 `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }`; :45-52 try `new DOMParser()` catch → `{ results: [], total: 0, error: 'DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime' }`. Live: `curl https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` → http=200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"}`. The other two edge shims are healthy: /api/search/opencontext?q=test → 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"hasMore":false}`; /api/search/openedition?q=test → 200 with results. The code comment at :45 shows the author anticipated this and shipped anyway.
findings.impact: A listed source silently never returns results, and because the shim answers 200 the coverage/credit math and the UI treat it as a healthy-but-empty adapter — users and API customers pay for a source that cannot work.
findings.fix_hint: Either parse the SRU XML with a regex/lightweight tokenizer (the existing src/adapters/_shared/xmlUtils.js pattern) or move Gallica into the Node `api/search/[source].js` dispatcher (8 Node files today, 12 cap → slots available). Add a live smoke assertion so a shim that returns `error` on a fixed query fails the post-deploy check.

findings.title: Preview deployments have no database env at all — Dependabot 'green' builds prove nothing about runtime, and migrate.mjs burns three failing Prisma runs per preview
findings.claim: POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING (and by inference POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL) is scoped to Production only, so every preview build fails schema validation, runs the fallback anyway, and ships a bundle whose auth/credits/checkout/webhook code cannot execute; a READY preview therefore says nothing about whether @auth/core 0.41.3 or prisma-adapter 2.11.3 actually work.
findings.evidence: Build logs of dpl_DE31RrgR8RNxBm4GvYMTJ5hwHMEE and dpl_94wrsdgkHC956DPsfG9wkH4st6R9: `Error code: P1012 … Environment variable not found: POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING. --> prisma/schema.prisma:13` for `migrate deploy` AND again for the `db execute` fallback, then `[migrate] SQL apply failed — NOT baselining`, then the build completes and the deployment is READY. scripts/migrate.mjs:47-63 has no `VERCEL_ENV` guard. package.json:9 runs migrate.mjs unconditionally in `build`.
findings.impact: The safety net that would justify merging a dependency PR (a preview you can sign into) does not exist; combined with auto-production deploys this makes every Dependabot merge a blind production experiment. Preview URLs shared for review also mislead reviewers (auth UI is dead there for an unrelated reason).
findings.fix_hint: Skip migrate.mjs unless `process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'production'` (one line at the top) so previews stop pretending to migrate; if preview auth is wanted, give previews their own throwaway Postgres (Neon free, or a Supabase branch on Pro) rather than pointing them at prod. Keep prod-only scoping for the real DB.

findings.title: Build-time env guards cannot fail the build; API_KEY_PEPPER/AUTH_SECRET throws hit only at cold start, and the blast radius is 6 of 8 Node functions
findings.claim: The 'throw at module load (deploy time)' comments are wrong about timing: Vite never imports api/, so a missing AUTH_SECRET or API_KEY_PEPPER produces a green deploy whose functions 500 on first invocation — the same silent-success shape as migrate.mjs's always-exit-0.
findings.evidence: api/_shared/crypto.js:56-60 throws when `NODE_ENV === 'production' && !API_KEY_PEPPER`; api/auth/handler.js:22-26 throws when AUTH_SECRET missing/short. Build log of dpl_2ZTVC6KJ shows only `prisma generate`, migrate.mjs, tailwind and `vite build` — no api/ module is evaluated. Importers of crypto.js: apiAuth.js, handlers/keys.js, handlers/settings.js; apiAuth.js is imported by auth.js, handlers/credits.js, meter.js, plans.js, search.js → functions affected: search, citations, ids (via meter), checkout (via auth.js), user/[resource], plus auth/handler for AUTH_SECRET; only stripe/webhook and the edge shims are immune. Both vars are set in prod today (live /api/search → 401, not 500). Node function inventory: 8 files (auth/handler, checkout, citations, ids, search, search/[source], stripe/webhook, user/[resource]); Vercel `lambdaRuntimeStats` reports nodejs:9 for the live deploy; cap 12; v0.45 adds 0 files + 1 daily cron (Hobby: daily-only cadence, allowed). docs/wiki/08-Build-Deploy/Build-Deploy.md still says of API_KEY_PEPPER 'there is no guard that fails startup' and shows vercel.json with 2 rewrites (now 7); .env.example:24,32,39,77 still reference the dead opencite.app domain.
findings.impact: An env-var mistake (e.g. re-creating the Vercel project during a DR, or rotating secrets) ships a green deploy that 500s on every authenticated route, and — as with the DB outage — nothing would notice. Docs mislead the operator about both the guard's existence and its timing.
findings.fix_hint: Add a `scripts/preflight.mjs` step to `build` that asserts the production env set (AUTH_SECRET≥32, API_KEY_PEPPER, SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, POSTGRES_* , AUTH_GOOGLE_*) when VERCEL_ENV==='production' and exits non-zero — this is the one place a build SHOULD fail. Fix the crypto.js/handler.js comments, refresh Build-Deploy.md's vercel.json/deps/pepper sections, and replace opencite.app in .env.example with citation.today.

market-gtm.summary: OpenCITE's paid proposition (origin-blind meta-search over free scholarly APIs at $0.0007-0.001/query) is priced below its own upstream cost since OpenAlex moved to mandatory keys + $0.001/search-call usage pricing in Feb 2026, and the server never sends an OpenAlex key, so the flagship source runs on a ~$0.10/day keyless allowance (~50 paid queries/day) before it 409s and every subsequent query is auto-discounted 50% by the coverage prorater. The free web app is fully unmetered client-side and already grants all sources, so the $5/$10 subscriptions sell nothing the free product withholds; pack buyers get a plan=free (core-only) key; Student is unpurchasable. Distribution is zero: stdio-only, npm-private MCP; no served OpenAPI/docs; site unindexed; and both Claude and ChatGPT directories require remote HTTPS+OAuth, a privacy policy, and disclosure/ownership of the upstream APIs that 'origin-blind' is designed to hide, while ChatGPT bans in-app checkout links (killing the v0.37 402-paywall funnel). Free competitors (paper-search-mcp 2.6k stars, 22 sources, MIT; 8+ OpenAlex MCPs; Consensus/Wiley/bioRxiv/PubMed official connectors) own the scholarly-search-for-agents niche; OpenCITE's genuine edges are heritage/Islamicate/regional breadth, one-contract citation formats + graph + ID resolution, and coverage-honest billing, none of which the marketing leads with. findings.title: Price point is 5-100x below every comparator and below upstream cost; free MIT alternatives cover the same sources
findings.claim: $0.67-1.00 per 1k queries is priced as if upstream were free and as if there were no free substitutes; both premises are false, so the margin is negative and the price signals 'toy' rather than 'cheapest credible grounding API'.

OpenAlex, Crossref, DOAJ, BASE, Europe PMC, CORE, installable via PyPI/Smithery/npx (https://github.com/openags/paper-search-mcp); 8+ OpenAlex MCP servers (https://github.com/topics/openalex). findings.impact: At list price, 1,000 pack buyers/month are needed to gross $10k, while each query loses money on OpenAlex alone; the free web app plus free MIT MCPs remove any reason for a scholarly-only developer to pay. Revenue potential of path (b) is near zero at this price.

Sell what the free MCPs lack (heritage/Islamicate sources, citation formats, coverage-honest refunds, hosted/no-install) rather than competing on OpenAlex wrapper price.

findings.title: 'Origin-blind' is a liability for every real distribution channel and for buyers who want provenance
findings.claim: Hiding the upstream source conflicts with Claude/ChatGPT directory rules (must disclose/own the underlying API), with attribution-required upstreams (CORE, Brave-style clauses), and with what grounding buyers select for (Consensus, Wiley, PubMed connectors all advertise their corpus), while protecting no real moat.

JASIST 2025 aggregation study: visible provenance is 'fundamental for judging quality and trustworthiness' (https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/asi.70006).

findings.fix_hint: Flip to origin-transparent: return `source` (and per-source attribution string) from publicResult.js; keep dedup/one-call/coverage as the value; re-admit CORE under its attribution terms; rewrite B1-B5 in TOS-items and the MCP/package descriptions. findings.title: Zero discoverability: MCP is stdio-only and npm-private, OpenAPI/docs are not served, domain is unindexed
findings.claim: No channel through which an agent developer could find or install the OpenCITE API/MCP exists today; every 2026 directory requires either a public remote MCP endpoint (Claude/ChatGPT) or a published package (Smithery/npm), and the site itself has no API docs page.
findings.evidence: mcp/package.json:4 '"private": true' (npm refuses to publish); mcp/src/server.js:19,87-91 StdioServerTransport only, no Streamable HTTP; `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencite%2fmcp` -> {"error":"Not found"}; `curl https://citation.today/openapi.json` and `/docs` return the SPA index.html (vercel.json:13 catch-all rewrite) so the OpenAPI spec generated by `npm run print-schemas` (mcp/README.md:88-98) is never published; public/robots.txt welcomes GPTBot/ClaudeBot but WebSearch `site:citation.today` returns no indexed pages. findings.claim: Public copy is contradictory and stale (free/no-paywall vs paid API; dead opencite.app link; v.13 architecture; roadmap prices $2.99/$9.99 + Base L2 micropayments that contradict plans.js; MCP description says 'ranked' after v0.44 removed ranking), while the genuine edges are never named.

legal-compliance.summary: OpenCITE is not legally ready to charge money, and two issues can reverse revenue rather than merely block it. First, the site sells a Stripe checkout with zero customer-facing legal surface: /terms and /privacy resolve to the SPA shell (identical md5 to /), the Footer has no legal links, the ToS is a self-labelled DRAFT that says "do not link", and the Stripe checkout session sets no consent or policy links — this fails Stripe's website checklist (refund/cancellation policy, privacy policy, contact, currency) and makes every dispute a loss. Second, OpenAlex now meters API usage at $0.001 per search call (verified live: cost_usd 0.001 on both search= and title.search filters); every /api/search fans out two such calls (OPENALEX + CURATED) with no server OpenAlex key, so each sold query costs ~$0.002 upstream against $0.00067-$0.001 revenue. The 24-adapter serverSafe billable set was only ToS-reviewed for 5 sources; Internet Archive (scholarship/research only), BASE (non-commercial, key-gated), BnF (Etalab attribution), Thaqalayn (third-party scraper API of unlicensed texts) and relayed PubMed abstracts all conflict with an origin-blind paid resale. Privacy exposure is real: Google OAuth tokens, email, search history and library are stored with no privacy policy, no account-deletion endpoint, and Vercel Analytics + Speed Insights are live despite README's "No tracking". The LICENSE (no hosted/commercial use) contradicts mcp/package.json MIT, the GitHub "Open-source" description, and "PRs welcome" without a CLA. Student plan and App Store copy advertise things that cannot be purchased or do not exist.

findings.title: OpenAlex metered pricing makes every sold query cost more upstream than it earns
findings.claim: Since Feb 2026 OpenAlex bills API usage per call; each /api/search query fires two OpenAlex search calls (OPENALEX + CURATED) at $0.001 each with no server API key, so upstream cost (~$0.002/query) exceeds the $0.00067-$0.001/query pack price and runs on the un-keyed demo budget.
findings.evidence: Live: `curl 'https://api.openalex.org/works?search=climate&per-page=1'` and `...?filter=title.search:climate&per-page=1` both return meta `"cost_usd": 0.001`. src/adapters/core/openalex.js:46 and src/adapters/core/curatedJournals.js:42 both call api.openalex.org/works?filter=...search with only `&mailto=` (openalex.js:30-31) — `grep -rn OPENALEX api .env.example` finds no OPENALEX_API_KEY anywhere server-side. Pack prices: src/constants/pricing.js:73-75 ($0.0010/$0.00083/$0.00067 per query). OpenAlex help center: 'A free API key raises your daily budget 10x'; CASRAI summary: ~$1/day free allowance per key, search calls $1.00 per 1,000, un-keyed path 'not suitable for production'.
findings.impact: Negative gross margin on the core source alone for every PAYG credit sold; on the un-keyed path the shared prod egress exhausts a small daily demo budget, after which OpenAlex (the largest core source) drops for all customers while credits keep being charged at near-full coverage (OpenAlex failure only lowers the band, it does not zero the charge).
findings.fix_hint: Register an OpenAlex API key, inject it server-side (serverKeys.js pattern) and pass `api_key` in openalex.js/curatedJournals.js; collapse the two OpenAlex calls into one per query (CURATED is an OpenAlex filter on ISSNs); re-price packs above ~$0.003/query or cap OpenAlex calls per query; add an upstream-cost line to plans.js so per-source metered cost is visible before enabling a source in the billable set.

findings.title: No published ToS, privacy, refund or contact surface behind a live Stripe checkout
findings.claim: The site accepts Stripe subscription and pack checkouts while displaying none of the policies Stripe's website checklist and card-network rules require: no terms, privacy, refund/cancellation policy, currency label, support contact or business address anywhere on citation.today.
findings.evidence: Footer at src/components/Layout.jsx:248-256 renders only 'Always verify citations...' — no legal links. `curl` https://citation.today/terms, /privacy, /tos, /legal all return the SPA shell (md5 502caecb... identical to /; vercel.json catch-all rewrite line 16-19). Bundle grep for 'terms of service|privacy policy|refund' = 0 hits. docs/wiki/11-Legal/Terms-of-Service.md:11-15 says 'DRAFT ... Do not link it from the live site'; Legal-Overview.md:49-58 lists L2 Privacy, L6, L7 DMCA, L8 footer links as 'not started'. api/checkout.js:101-112 creates the session with no `consent_collection`, no policy URLs; pricing copy shows '$5' with no currency code (src/constants/pricing.js:37,54). Stripe docs 'Website checklist' (docs.stripe.com/get-started/checklist/website) require description, purchase currency, customer-service contact, refund + cancellation policy, privacy policy; 'If your website doesn't include sufficient information about your fulfillment policies, we might request that you add it.'
findings.impact: Stripe account review can impose reserves, payout holds or termination; every chargeback on a digital-credit sale is lost by default with no posted refund/cancellation policy (revenue reversal + dispute fees); no contractual limitation of liability or anti-circumvention terms actually bind any paying user because nothing was accepted.
findings.fix_hint: Publish ToS + Privacy + Refund/Cancellation + Contact (email, DMCA agent) as static routes (public/legal/*.html or SPA routes excluded from the catch-all), link them in Footer and AuthModal, set `consent_collection: { terms_of_service: 'required' }` and Dashboard 'Public details' policy URLs, show 'USD' next to prices. Counsel review of the draft ToS is the gating item (L1).

findings.title: Non-refundable credits with no cancellation path; refunds and disputes never claw back credits
findings.claim: ToS §5 declares credits non-refundable and there is no user-facing cancel/portal, which conflicts with California ARL and EU Consumer Rights Directive obligations; and the webhook ignores charge.refunded / charge.dispute.* so a refunded or charged-back pack leaves the credits spendable.
findings.evidence: docs/wiki/11-Legal/Terms-of-Service.md:71 'Credits are non-refundable'. `grep -rn 'billingPortal|portal' api src` = no results; PricingPanel (src/components/Panels.jsx:183-290) has no cancel/manage button. api/stripe/webhook.js:124-198 handles only checkout.session.completed, RENEWAL_EVENTS, customer.subscription.updated/deleted, invoice.payment_failed — no charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, or credit reversal. Stripe checklist requires a cancellation policy for subscriptions; CA Bus. & Prof. Code 17602 requires online cancellation and affirmative consent to auto-renewal (non-compliant subscriptions are 'unconditional gifts'); EU CRD Art. 9/14 gives 14-day withdrawal on digital services with pro-rata refund.
findings.impact: Chargebacks reverse revenue while the customer keeps 10k-300k credits (double loss); statutory non-compliance in CA/EU can void subscription charges entirely; Stripe disputes without a posted policy are lost by default.
findings.fix_hint: Add a Stripe Customer Portal link (stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create) in the Plans panel; handle charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created in the webhook by decrementing the pack's credits (floor at 0) and flagging the account; rewrite ToS §5 to a lawful policy (14-day withdrawal for unused credits, pro-rata for subscriptions); add explicit auto-renewal consent text at checkout.

findings.title: Billable serverSafe set includes sources whose terms forbid commercial/origin-blind resale
findings.claim: 24 adapters are serverSafe (billable to paid/all-tier plans) but TOS-items.md reviewed only 5; at least Internet Archive, BASE, BnF, Thaqalayn, Open Library and relayed PubMed abstracts conflict with a paid, origin-blind API that strips attribution.

Internet Archive ToS (archive.org/about/terms.php, quoted in IA forum post 1101677): access to Collections 'granted for scholarship and research purposes only' — src/adapters/extensions/internetArchive.js:165 serverSafe:true, hits be-api.us.archive.org FTS (line 64). BASE: API is key/IP-gated and offered 'for non-commercial services' (api.base-search.net; searxng issue #5283) — src/adapters/extensions/base.js:32 serverSafe:true, line 44 calls the interface. BnF catalogue SRU metadata under Etalab Licence Ouverte requiring the source 'Bibliothèque nationale de France' be cited (api.bnf.fr CGU) — src/adapters/extensions/bnfApi.js:18,25; origin-blind contract (TOS-items B1/D6) forbids exactly that attribution. findings.fix_hint: Apply the D6 filter to all 24 sources and record each in TOS-items.md; flip serverSafe to false for IA, BASE, BnF, Thaqalayn, Open Library (or obtain written licenses); drop `abstract` from the paid contract for NCBI-origin cards or truncate to snippet; keep those sources browser-only like CORE/NDLI.

findings.title: Personal data stored with no privacy policy, no deletion path, and analytics contradicting the 'No tracking' claim
findings.claim: OpenCITE stores Google OAuth refresh/access/id tokens, email, name, avatar, search history, library, Stripe customer ids and encrypted third-party API keys with no privacy notice, no account-deletion or export endpoint, while README claims 'No tracking' and the live bundle loads Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights.
findings.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:73-77 Account.refresh_token/access_token/id_token stored as plaintext @db.Text; :20-23 email/name/image; :109-119 search_history (query per user); :123-134 library_items; :26 stripe_customer_id; :45 settings encrypted blob (api/_shared/handlers/settings.js:5-7). api/user/[resource].js:20 HANDLERS = credits/history/keys/library/settings only — no delete-account or data export; history/library DELETE exist but the User/Account rows and Stripe link cannot be erased by the user. README.md:7 'No account required. No tracking.' vs src/App.jsx:2-3,460-461 mounting <Analytics/> and <SpeedInsights/>; live bundle contains '_vercel/insights', '_vercel/speed-insights', 'va.vercel-scripts'. Legal-Overview.md:52 L2 Privacy Policy 'not started'. Google OAuth production policy requires a homepage with linked privacy policy and ToS, and the same policy URL on the consent screen (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/policies).
findings.impact: GDPR Art. 13/17/20 and CCPA notice/deletion rights are unmet for EU/CA users the moment money changes hands (Stripe transactions expand the data set); Google can flag the OAuth app as unverified or suspend it, killing the only sign-in and therefore checkout; the false 'No tracking' statement is a deceptive-practice exposure.
findings.fix_hint: Publish a privacy policy naming Stripe, Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights, Supabase, Google OAuth and each upstream; add DELETE /api/user/account (cascade via Prisma onDelete, Stripe customer delete, subscription cancel) and a JSON export; either remove Analytics/SpeedInsights or correct README; set the privacy URL on the Google consent screen.

findings.title: Digital sales with no tax collection or customer location capture
findings.claim: Checkout sessions are created with no automatic_tax, billing_address_collection or tax_id_collection, so VAT/GST/sales tax on cross-border digital services is neither charged nor tracked.
findings.evidence: api/checkout.js:101-112 `stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ mode, customer, client_reference_id, line_items, metadata, allow_promotion_codes, success_url, cancel_url })` — `grep -rn 'automatic_tax|tax_id' api` returns nothing. Stripe guidance: EU VAT applies to B2C digital services based on customer location from the first sale for non-EU sellers (stripe.com/guides/introduction-to-eu-vat-and-european-vat-oss); several US states tax SaaS.
findings.impact: Uncollected VAT/GST becomes the operator's liability (out of the $5/$10 price), with penalties; inference on jurisdictional thresholds — exposure grows with volume but EU B2C has no threshold for a US seller.
findings.fix_hint: Enable Stripe Tax and pass `automatic_tax: { enabled: true }` + `billing_address_collection: 'required'` + `tax_id_collection: { enabled: true }`; register for OSS/non-Union scheme when EU sales begin.

findings.title: Upstream identification policies violated by spoofed or absent User-Agent and missing NCBI tool/email
findings.claim: Server-side requests either spoof a Chrome desktop User-Agent or send none, and NCBI E-utilities calls omit the required tool/email parameters, breaching NCBI, Open Library and Wikimedia access policies for automated clients.
findings.evidence: api/proxy.js:100 and src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:35 hard-code 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0...) Chrome/122' as User-Agent. src/adapters/extensions/ncbi.js:53,61,62 call esearch/esummary/efetch with no `tool=`/`email=`/`api_key=` (search.js:341 passes NCBI_API_KEY only to the env-gated canonicalizer, not the adapter). Open Library requires 'User-Agent: AppName (contact@email)' and rate-limits/blocks otherwise (openlibrary.org/developers/api); NCBI: 'Use the URL parameter email, and tool for distributed software' (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies). Only wikidata.js:7 sets a proper Api-User-Agent. OPENCITE_MAILTO is commented out in .env.example:77 so Crossref polite pool depends on an unverified prod env var.
findings.impact: A single IP block of Vercel's shared egress silently removes NCBI/Open Library/IA for every paying customer (TOS-items D2), while coverage-prorated billing still charges; UA spoofing weakens any good-faith defence in an upstream dispute.
findings.fix_hint: Set one honest UA 'OpenCITE/<ver> (https://citation.today; mailto:<role address>)' in a shared fetch wrapper; append tool=opencite&email=<role>&api_key=NCBI_API_KEY in ncbi.js; verify OPENCITE_MAILTO is set in Vercel prod.

findings.title: LICENSE contradicts mcp/ MIT, the 'Open-source' GitHub description, and 'PRs welcome' with no CLA
findings.claim: The root license defines 'Software' as all associated source and forbids hosting and commercial use, yet mcp/package.json declares MIT with no license file, the GitHub description calls the project open-source, and the README invites PRs while the license grants Shahbaz no rights in contributors' code.
findings.evidence: LICENSE:8-10 'Software means OpenCITE and all associated source code'; :62-73 prohibit Hosted Services and Commercial Use; :43-53 grant rights only from Licensor to You (no inbound contributor grant). mcp/package.json:7 `"license": "MIT"`; `git ls-files | grep -i license` shows only the root LICENSE (no mcp/LICENSE). `gh api repos/Zabhahs/OpenCite` description: 'Open-source, modular citation generator...', license spdx_id NOASSERTION, homepage 'opencitedeploy.vercel.app'. README.md:199-201 'Issues and PRs welcome'. README.md:217 says Copyright 2026, LICENSE:2 says 2025.
findings.impact: Any merged outside PR is code the operator has no commercial/hosting license to (the license only flows outward), tainting the paid hosted service; 'open-source' + non-OSI license is a misrepresentation that invites forks that then violate the license; MIT on mcp/ arguably licenses the origin-blind schema/CLI for competitors while the root license says otherwise.
findings.fix_hint: Decide one posture: either add mcp/LICENSE (MIT) and carve mcp/ out of the root LICENSE definition, or make mcp/ source-available too; add a CLA/DCO with an explicit commercial grant before accepting PRs; fix the GitHub description/homepage and align copyright years.

docs-integrity.summary: The wiki, its machine twin, the GitHub mirror, README and the repo-tracked memory are four documentation surfaces that now disagree with each other and with the working tree. The v0.44 sprint's T7 doc pass was only half-done: Pipeline/Known-Defects/Search-Endpoint/System-Architecture were rewritten to pass-through reality, but the findings ledger was never re-statused (0 records are `moot`; F-200 confirmed, F-205 spike-complete, F-209 open, F-405 open though fixed), Health-Dashboard/Adapter-Health-Matrix/Security/Bugs/Proxy/Shared-Modules/Glossary/Tech-Stack/UI-Map/What-We-Did-Well still describe the deleted BM25F/RRF/gate engine and pre-v0.39 security gaps as live, and docs/wiki-gh was last generated at 4f4849b (pre-v0.44) so GitHub readers get 36 deleted pages and no Pipeline/WIKI-RULES. findings.title: Gallica Edge route has returned a hard-coded 'DOMParser unavailable' error since 2026-05-21 and no finding tracks it
findings.claim: The Gallica per-source route runs on the Edge runtime and calls `new DOMParser()`, which the code itself predicts is unavailable; every request returns 200 with zero results, so Gallica has never worked in prod and the browser adapter that depends on it always shows nothing.
findings.evidence: api/search/gallica.js:3 `runtime: 'edge'`, :45 comment 'DOMParser may not exist in Vercel Edge V8', :48 `new DOMParser()`, :52 returns `{results: [], error: 'DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime'}` with status 200. `git log -- api/search/gallica.js` → 0c9b480 (05-29), 1918934 (05-26), 0d2751e (05-21). Live: `curl -s https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` → `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"} [200]` (opencontext/openedition edge routes return data). src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:26 fetches this relative URL. `grep -niE 'gallica|DOMParser' docs/wiki/_machine/findings.json` → only F-112 (transport audit, v0.38 T8) and F-410; no finding for the breakage — v0.38 T8 audited this file's transport (findings.json:177) without noticing it never returns results.
findings.impact: Users see a dead source in every browser search (silent 0 results); the coverage/adapter-health story in the wiki counts Gallica as live; the v0.38 circuit-breaker cannot catch it because the route returns 200 not an error.
findings.fix_hint: Parse the SRU XML without DOMParser (regex or a tiny XML tokenizer already used in xmlUtils) or move the route into the Node `api/search/[source].js` dispatcher (does not add a function — the 12-function cap is already hit). Mint a finding id and add it to the ledger.
